articles.title: BJP looted over 100 seats, we will bounce back: Mamata Banerjee
articles.snippet: The TMC supremo alleged that the 'EC’s activities with the help of central forces in connivance with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah were illegal'
articles.author: PTI
articles.description: The TMC supremo alleged that the 'EC’s activities with the help of central forces in connivance with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah were illegal'
articles.body: TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee on Monday termed the BJP’s landslide victory in the state polls ”immoral” and alleged that the mandate in more than 100 seats was ”looted”.    ”We will bounce back,” she said while walking out of the counting centre at her Bhabanipur Assembly constituency.Banerjee had reached the counting centre at Sakhawat Memorial Government Girls’ High School on Lord Sinha Road in the afternoon amid allegations by the Trinamool Congress that one of its counting agents had been forced out of the venue.    As she came out of the centre, the TMC supremo was greeted by ”Jai Shree Ram” slogans by BJP supporters emboldened by their party’s sweep in the polls, even more sweetened by the 10,994 lead Suvendu Adhikari gained in Banerjee’s Bhabanipur constituency.A visibly distraught Banerjee told reporters that the BJP’s victory was ”immoral”. ”They have looted more than 100 seats,” she alleged.    The TMC supremo alleged that the ”EC’s activities with the help of central forces in connivance with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah were illegal”.Alleging that she received flak ”for speaking out against the EC’s malpractices”, the TMC supremo said, ”I lodged a complaint with Chief Electoral Officer Manoj Agarwal, but to no avail.” ”The CCTV was switched off while our agents were not allowed to be inside the counting centre,” she claimed.

articles.title: West Bengal Assembly polls: List of key winners, losers
articles.snippet: The BJP won in 190 seats and was leading in 17 assembly constituencies while the TMC won 64 seats and was leading in 17 assembly constituencies
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: The BJP won in 190 seats and was leading in 17 assembly constituencies while the TMC won 64 seats and was leading in 17 assembly constituencies
articles.body: While the counting of votes is still underway in West Bengal, the BJP looks set to form the government in Bengal, bringing an end to the 15-year rule of the Trinamool Congress.    As of 10pm on Monday (May 4), the BJP won in 190 seats and was leading in 17 assembly constituencies while the TMC won 64 seats and was leading in 17 assembly constituencies. While the decision is awaited on quite a few number of assembly seats, we take a look at the key winners and losers so far.    WINNERS    Suvendu Adhikari    If the victory in the West Bengal elections was sweet for BJP, it was sweeter for its Leader of Opposition Suvendu Adhikari. The BJP strongman retained his constituency Nandigram by defeating TMC's Pabitra Kar by a margin of 9,665 votes after 19 rounds of voting.    While Adhikari was relishing his Nandigram win, what topped as the cherry on the cake for the BJP leader was him wresting the much coveted Bhabanipur assembly constituency from West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee. Adhikari defeated Banerjee by a margin of over 15,000 votes, handing a severe defeat to the TMC supremo in her own home constituency.    Agnimitra Paul    Agnimitra Paul, the BJP candidate from Asansol Dakshin, won the assembly constituency by winning 1,19,582 votes. She defeated TMC's Tapas Banerjee by a margin of over 40,000 votes.    &quot;Tsunami will come today, not just a wave. The people of Bengal have called for a tsunami by voting over 92 per cent. In front of this, every leader will be swept away, no matter how big or influential,&quot; Paul told ANI.    Ratna Debnath    Perhaps besides Suvendu Adhikari, the other most watched out BJP candidate this election was Ratna Debnath, the mother of RG Kar rape and murder victim and the party's candidate from the Panihati assembly constituency.    Debnath, a debutant with no political history or background, marked a significant victory, securing 87,977 votes. She defeated TMC's Tirthankar Ghosh by a margin of 28,000 votes.    After she was declared the winner, Debnath said, &quot;This victory is the victory of the people of Panihati, of the entire Bengal. I dedicate this victory to Prime Minister Modi. I have been able to free the people from the misgovernance of the Ghosh family, for which I thank the people; I could not have done this alone. This victory has been achieved because of the people of Panihati.&quot;    Dilip Ghosh    Among the standout performers, Dilip Ghosh returned to the Assembly from Kharagpur Sadar with a margin of over 26,000 votes, staging a strong comeback after his 2024 Lok Sabha defeat.    He defeated the TMC's Pradip Sarkar by a margin of over 30,000 votes. &quot;... The people of Bengal have blessed the BJP. Prime Minister Modi had called for five years to transform Bengal, and the people placed their trust in him... For years, Mamata Banerjee relied only on accusations, and Bengal fell behind. Now, the people want work, not blame...,&quot; said Ghosh after his election victory.    Arup Roy    Arup Roy, the TMC candidate from Howrah Madhya, handed a crushing defeat to BJP's Biplab Kumar Mandal, winning the assembly seat by a margin of 16,083 votes.    Humayun Kabir    Humayun Kabir, the former TMC leader who was ousted from the party for wanting to construct a Babri Masjid style mosque in Murshidabad, has won from both Nowda and Rejinagar assembly seats.    After collecting his winning certificate, Kabir, who floated the Aam Janata Unnayan Party to fight the West Bengal Assembly elections, said, &quot;I am very happy... For the first time in the politics of West Bengal, this has happened. I have won both seats.&quot;    LOSERS     Mamata Banerjee    Mamata Banerjee, the powerhouse of the Trinamool Congress who was setting to return as West Bengal's Chief Minister for the fourth consecutive time, suffered a double blow.    Not only has her party lost the West Bengal Assembly elections, she also lost her home turf Bhabanipur assembly constituency to her former aide and now BJP's Leader of Opposition Suvendu Adhikari. Banerjee alleged that the BJP stole 100 seats from the Election Commission, a claim that received support from senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi.    Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury    Senior Congress leader Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury, who entered West Bengal's electoral fray after nearly 30 years, was confident of winning the elections this time. He fought the election from the Barhampore assembly constituency in Murshidabad district. However, he lost to Subrata Maitra, the candidate pitted by the BJP here, by a margin of 17,548 votes.    Shashi Panja    West Bengal's women and child welfare minister Shashi Panja was defeated by BJP's Purnima Chakraborty by 14,633 votes in Shyampukur assembly constituency. Chakraborty secured 60,248 votes, while Panja got 45,615 votes.    Chandrima Bhattacharya    West Bengal's state Finance minister Chandrima Bhattacharya was defeated in Dum Dum Uttar constituency by 26,404 votes by BJP's Sourav Sikdar.    Debabrata Majumdar    Debabrata Majumdar (Malay), the candidate fielded by TMC from Jadavpur assembly constituency, was defeated by BJP's Sarbori Mukherjee by 27,716 votes.    Udayan Guha    TMC's north Bengal leader and minister Udayan Guha lost the Dinhata seat to BJP's Ajay Ray by over 17,000 votes.    Goutam Deb    Goutam Deb, the TMC candidate from Siliguri assembly constituency and also the mayor of Siliguri Municipal Corporation, lost by a huge margin of 73,192 votes to BJP's Sankar Ghosh.

articles.title: BJP’s next big test: After Bengal sweep, focus shifts to 2027 showdown in UP, Gujarat, Punjab,...
articles.snippet: The party has already begun groundwork for these elections, with BJP president Nitin Nabin initiating preparations and holding strategy meetings across key states
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: The party has already begun groundwork for these elections, with BJP president Nitin Nabin initiating preparations and holding strategy meetings across key states
articles.body: With a strong showing in the West Bengal and Assam Assembly elections, the BJP is now turning its focus to the next big electoral test in 2027, when seven states, including Goa, Manipur, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh, go to polls.    The party has already begun groundwork for these elections, with BJP president Nitin Nabin initiating preparations and holding strategy meetings across key states. “As the elections in the five states have concluded, the party will now shift its focus to the polls due to be held in seven states next year. Some groundworks have already been set in motion by party president Nitin Nabin. It will now be ramped up,” a BJP source said.    Nabin has visited Goa, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh to engage with party leaders and map out electoral strategies, and is expected to visit Uttarakhand soon. The BJP is currently in power in Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Uttarakhand, Manipur and Goa, while Punjab is ruled by AAP and Himachal Pradesh by the Congress.    Speaking at a celebration event at the BJP headquarters following the party’s recent poll performance, Nabin credited the results to public faith in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership.    “From Gangotri to Ganga Sagar, the NDA-BJP government is being formed. This is not only a geographical expansion but also an expansion of people's trust in our leadership and his vision,” he said.    “On this day, I assure my beloved leader and illustrious prime minister of the country, Narendra Modi ji of this: 'You lead the way. The workers of the Bharatiya Janata Party have already set about preparing for the times ahead with full determination and a spirit of dedication,” Nabin declared.    The BJP’s recent performance saw it poised to form its first government in West Bengal, leading in more than 200 seats in the 294-member assembly, while in Assam, the BJP-led NDA crossed the majority mark comfortably. In Tamil Nadu, however, the BJP won just one seat, while in Kerala, it made gains by securing three seats in a state where it has historically struggled for a foothold.    *With Agency Inputs

articles.title: RG Kar victim's mother scripts history: Ratna Debnath wins Panihati for BJP, ends TMC rule with...
articles.snippet: Debnath's rise from a grieving mother to a political figure became a defining narrative of the contest, symbolising a shift in voter sentiment in the constituency.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: Debnath's rise from a grieving mother to a political figure became a defining narrative of the contest, symbolising a shift in voter sentiment in the constituency.
articles.body: In a major electoral upset in West Bengal, BJP candidate Ratna Debnath secured a decisive victory in the Panihati Assembly constituency, defeating the Trinamool Congress (TMC) and ending its long-standing hold on the seat since 2011.    According to final results after 13 rounds of counting, Debnath polled 87,977 votes, winning by a margin of 28,836 votes over TMC candidate Tirthankar Ghosh, who secured 59,141 votes. CPI(M) candidate Kalatan Dasgupta finished a distant third with 24,032 votes.    The result marks a significant political shift in Panihati, long considered a TMC bastion, and comes amid broader gains for the BJP across West Bengal in the 2026 Assembly elections.    Debnath, whose campaign was shaped by her personal tragedy linked to the RG Kar Medical College rape and murder case, framed her victory as a mandate rooted in justice and women’s safety.    Speaking after her win, Ratna Debnath said, “All my co-workers, I would like to thank them first, all the media friends, who are with me for so many days, I thank all of you. All the residents of Panihati, the way they stood with me, I would like to express my gratitude and Prime Minister Modi ji who gave me the nomination, I would like to express my gratitude to him. The whole world is watching towards Panihati...”    Her husband, Sekhar Ranjan Debnath, also celebrated the outcome, saying, “We have won by around 30,000 margin. I would like to thank the residents of Panihati for voting in favour of us. I had said earlier that our candidate will win, Residents of Panihati will win and in West Bengal lotus will bloom...”    Ratna Debnath herself said, “This victory is the victory of the people of Panihati, of the entire Bengal. I dedicate this victory to Prime Minister Modi. I have been able to free the people from the misgovernance of the Ghosh family, for which I thank the people; I could not have done this alone. This victory has been achieved because of the people of Panihati.”    During the campaign, she had described her political fight in deeply personal terms, saying, “This election is not just about votes. It is a fight for justice, a fight for my daughter, a fight for the safety of women in Bengal.”    After the result, she reiterated, “The people of Panihati are with me, and this vote is for my daughter, for justice, and for the women of Bengal who have long suffered under a government that ignores their cries.”    She further alleged pressure during campaigning, stating, “The people of Bengal are fed up with the TMC. This election is their chance to fight back,” and claimed she was “surrounded and threatened by TMC workers,” adding that it only strengthened her resolve.    Her rise from a grieving mother to a political figure became a defining narrative of the contest, symbolising a shift in voter sentiment in the constituency.

articles.description: Moneycontrol takes a look at the biggest winners and losers of the 2026 battle of states
articles.body: The Election Commission declared the results of the 2026 state assembly elections held across West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Assam and Puducherry on May 4.    Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress’ bid to return to power for the fourth time in West Bengal failed miserably, with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) clinched a historic mandate.    In Tamil Nadu, actor-turned-politician Vijay made an unexpected debut in the state’s politics with TVK leading in over 100 seats, while the two Dravidian forces DMK and AIADMK were relegated to second and third spot, respectively.    Himanta Biswa Sarma will return to power in Assam for another term as the state’s chief minister, while the NDA will maintain its power in Puducherry. Congress will form its government in Kerala, with Pinarayi Vijayan’s CPI(M) set for a massive defeat. articles.title: 'Janata janardan verdict': Suvendu Adhikari calls Bhabanipur win mandate for 'Sonar Bangla'
articles.snippet: The statement came hours after Adhikari secured a landmark win in Bhabanipur, defeating TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee by 15,105 votes after 20 rounds of counting.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: The statement came hours after Adhikari secured a landmark win in Bhabanipur, defeating TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee by 15,105 votes after 20 rounds of counting.
articles.body: In a dramatic post-election statement following his high-profile victory in West Bengal’s Bhabanipur constituency, BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari, on Monday evening, said the 2026 Assembly mandate reflected a “resounding triumph” for the people of the state, framing the result as a turning point in Bengal’s political trajectory.    Addressing supporters, Adhikari wrote, “With a heart overflowing with humility and profound gratitude, I bow before the ‘Janata-Janardan’ of West Bengal.”    He framed the outcome as a broader ideological shift, stating, “Today’s historic mandate is not just a victory for the Bharatiya Janata Party; it is a resounding triumph for every Citizen, every Sanatani who dreamt of a ‘Sonar Bangla’ where Lotus Blooms in the Hindu Homeland carved out by Param Poojaniya Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee.”    With a heart overflowing with humility and profound gratitude, I bow before the ‘Janata-Janardan’ of West Bengal.  Today’s historic mandate is not just a victory for the Bharatiya Janata Party; it is a resounding triumph for every Citizen, every Sanatani who dreamt of a ‘Sonar…  — Suvendu Adhikari (@SuvenduWB) May 4, 2026      Claiming a decisive public verdict, he added, “The People of West Bengal have spoken, and their voice has ushered in a new dawn of hope.”    Adhikari expressed personal gratitude to voters in key constituencies, saying, “I am eternally indebted to the brave and resilient people of Nandigram and Bhabanipur… Your blessings is my greatest strength.”    He reserved strong praise for the top BJP leadership, stating, “This Monumental Victory would not have been possible without the tireless guidance of our Leader Hon’ble PM Shri Narendra Modi Ji… Hon’ble Home Minister Shri Amit Shah Ji, your indomitable will, strategic brilliance, and constant encouragement have been the backbone of our struggle.”    He also thanked senior party leaders, including Nitin Nabin, JP Nadda, Sunil Bansal, Bhupender Yadav, Amit Malviya, Samik Bhattacharya, and state BJP cadres, calling party workers the “real heroes” of the electoral battle.    “To our brave Karyakartas who lost their lives… this victory belongs to your sacrifice and sweat,” he said, adding that the party would now focus on governance and development in the state.    “We now move forward with a spirit of service, ready to build a West Bengal where peace prevails and the State moves towards progress and development,” he wrote, concluding with religious chants: “Joy Maa Tara, Joy Maa Kaali, Joy Maa Durga, Jai Shri Ram.”    The statement came hours after Adhikari secured a landmark win in Bhabanipur, defeating TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee by 15,105 votes after 20 rounds of counting. He polled 73,917 votes against Banerjee’s 58,812.    The result is being seen as one of the defining moments of the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections, marking a major political setback for the TMC and reinforcing Adhikari’s position as the BJP’s principal challenger in the state.

articles.title: 'Axis My India' accurately predicts TVK's stunning win; pollsters get WB, Assam, Kerala right
articles.snippet: Axis My India had decided not to give an exit poll for West Bengal, citing voters' non-response leading to incomplete sampling.
articles.author: PTI
articles.description: Axis My India had decided not to give an exit poll for West Bengal, citing voters' non-response leading to incomplete sampling.
articles.body: Most exit polls on West Bengal, Assam, Kerala and Puducherry got their predictions right but one pollster that stood out was 'Axis My India' with its accurate forecast of TVK's sensational election debut in Tamil Nadu.    While most exit polls got the direction of the West Bengal polls right, Today's Chanakya and Praja Poll got the scale of the BJP's win right. Praja Poll predicted a big win for the BJP, forecasting 178-208 seats for it. Today's Chanakya forecast 192 seats for the BJP and 100 for the TMC in West Bengal with a margin of error of 11 seats.    The BJP was set for a decisive win over the TMC in long-elusive West Bengal and headed for another term in Assam while actor-politician Vijay's TVK made a stunning debut in Tamil Nadu as the largest single party in terms of seats won or led.    As votes were counted for assembly elections in West Bengal, Assam, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry, Election Commission trends showed a wipeout of the Left and a solitary win for the Congress that has been battling diminishing electoral returns. That silver lining for the opposition party came from Kerala where the Congress-led UDF won or was leading in 101 of the 140 Assembly seats while the CPM-led ruling Left Democratic Front (LDF) was ahead in just under 40 constituencies.    The cynosure of Election 2026, however, was West Bengal, the eastern state where the Trinamool Congress (TMC) was eyeing a fourth straight term in its only bastion.    In Tamil Nadu, two exit polls had caught everyone's eye as they had predicted a hung House. Axis My India had forecast 92-110 seats for the ruling DMK-led alliance, 22-23 for the AIADMK plus and 98-120 for the TVK, which was making its poll debut. Kamakhya Analytics forecast 78-95 seats for the DMK plus, 68-84 for the AIADMK plus and 67-81 for the TVK.    Actor-turned-politician Vijay's TVK made a stunning debut in Tamil Nadu, becoming the single largest party in terms of seats won or led, though it fell short of securing the majority mark of 118 in the state assembly of 234 seats.    Several polls wrongly predicted a big win for the DMK with the People's Pulse predicting 125-145 for the DMK-led alliance, 65-80 for AIADMK-BJP and 18-24 for the TVK.    While Matrize forecast that the DMK-Congress would get 122-132, AIADMK plus 87-100 and TVK 10-12, P-Marq predicted 125-145 for DMK plus, 65-85 for the AIADMK and 16-26 for the TVK.    JVC is the only pollster that has predicted an AIADMK win, forecasting 128-147 seats for AIADMK plus. It also forecast 75-95 for DMK plus and 18-15 for the TVK.    Praja polls predicted 148-168 seats for DMK plus, 61-81 for the AIADMK and 1-9 for the TVK.    Peoples Insight forecast 120-140 seats for DMK plus, 60-70 for the AIADMK and 30-40 for the TVK.    Tamil Nadu has 234 seats with the magic mark being 118.    Several exit polls predicted a thumping victory for the BJP in Assam and West Bengal, while projecting a comeback by the Congress-led UDF in Kerala after 10 years.    Almost all forecast a return to power for the AINRC-led NDA government in Puducherry.    In West Bengal, while most exit polls predicted a BJP win, two pollsters -- People's Pulse and Janmat polls -- predicted a big win for Mamata Banerjee-led TMC. People's Pulse predicted that the TMC would get 177-187 seats, BJP 95-110, Left Front 0-1 and the Congress 1-3. The Janmat polls forecast 195-205 for the TMC and 80-90 for the BJP plus and 1-3 for the Congress.    Most polls gave the BJP an edge or a victory in West Bengal. Matrize said it is likely to get 146-161 seats, while the TMC would get 125-140 seats.    P-Marq predicted 150-175 for the BJP and 118-138 for the TMC.    While Poll Diary forecast 142-171 seats to the BJP, 99-127 to the TMC and 3-5 to the Congress, Praja Poll predicted a big win for the BJP, forecasting 178-208 seats for it. Praja Poll said the TMC would get 85-110 seats. West Bengal has a total of 294 seats with the majority mark being 148.    Axis My India had decided not to give an exit poll for West Bengal, citing voters' non-response leading to incomplete sampling.    In Assam, Axis My India predicted a sweep for the BJP, forecasting 88-100 seats for the BJP and its allies and 24-36 seats for the Congress and its partners.    People's Pulse predicted that the NDA would get 68-72 seats in Assam while the Congress plus would secure in the range of 22-26 seats.    Matrize said the NDA is likely to get between 85-95 seats and the Congress and its allies 25-32.    Pollster JVC projected that the BJP plus would get 88-101 seats and the Congress and its allies 23-33 seats.    While Kamakhya Analytics predicted 85-95 seats for the BJP and its allies and 26-39 seats for the Congress and its allies, People's Insight forecast 88-96 seats for the NDA and 30-34 for the Congress in Assam.    In Kerala, Axis My India forecast that the UDF would get 78-90 seats, LDF 49-62 and NDA 0-3.    People's Pulse predicted that the Congress-led UDF would get 75-85 seats, the LDF 55-65 and the NDA 0-3.    Matrize forecast 60-65 seats for the LDF, 70-75 seats for the UDF and 3-5 seats for the NDA. Kerala Assembly has a total of 140 seats with the magic mark being 71.

articles.title: Jhal Muri moment: Nirmala Sitharaman celebrates BJP victory in West Bengal, says ‘khela shesh’
articles.snippet: In a post on X, Nirmala Sitharaman thanked voters for backing the BJP and described the result as the end of the Trinamool Congress rule
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: In a post on X, Nirmala Sitharaman thanked voters for backing the BJP and described the result as the end of the Trinamool Congress rule
articles.body: Union Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday hailed the Bharatiya Janata Party’s strong performance in the West Bengal Assembly elections, celebrating the moment with a bowl of jhal muri as the party won 177 seats and led in 31.    In a post on X, Nirmala Sitharaman thanked voters for backing the BJP and described the result as the end of the Trinamool Congress rule. “Immense gratitude to the people of West Bengal, for choosing BJP with hope and courage. People have chosen to end the oppressive AITC regime that betrayed Maa, Mati, Manush. This historic win of the BJP belongs to the countless karyakartas and leaders whose selfless struggle, sacrifice and courage brought the much-needed change. Under PM Narendra Modi ji, Bengal will rise again as one of India's leading states. For the TMC regime of fear, appeasement and protection of infiltrators, it is Khela Shesh (game over). Surely a day to celebrate with Jhaal Muri,” she wrote.    Immense gratitude to the people of West Bengal, for choosing BJP with hope and courage.    People have chosen to end the oppressive @AITCOfficial regime that betrayed Maa, Mati, Manush.    This historic win of @BJP4Bengal belongs to the countless karyakartas and leaders whose… pic.twitter.com/lK9DdBlIub  — Nirmala Sitharaman (@nsitharaman) May 4, 2026      Earlier, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, addressing party workers at the BJP headquarters, called for a forward-looking approach following the party’s performance.    “Today, when the BJP has won, the focus should be on change, not revenge. The focus should be on the future, not fear. I appeal to the workers of all political parties: let's end this endless cycle of violence once and for all,” he said.    Referring to past election violence in the state, Modi added, “This Bengal election has been very special for another reason as well. You must remember what kind of news used to come during Bengal elections. Violence, fear, and deaths of innocent people. But this time, the entire country heard a new piece of news that peaceful voting took place in West Bengal. For the first time, not a single innocent citizen lost their life in election violence. In this grand festival of democracy, it was not the sound of guns, but the voice of the people that echoed. For the first time, it was not fear, but democracy that triumphed.”    *With Agency Inputs

articles.title: 'Assam, Bengal elections stolen': Rahul Gandhi slams BJP, EC; cites repeated 'playbook'
articles.snippet: In a strongly worded post on X, Gandhi targeted both the ruling BJP and the Election Commission of India, echoing concerns earlier raised by TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: In a strongly worded post on X, Gandhi targeted both the ruling BJP and the Election Commission of India, echoing concerns earlier raised by TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee.
articles.body: Rahul Gandhi on Monday alleged large-scale electoral irregularities in the 2026 Assembly elections, claiming that outcomes in key states, including West Bengal and Assam, had been “stolen” with alleged institutional backing.    In a strongly worded post on X, Gandhi targeted both the ruling BJP and the Election Commission of India, echoing concerns earlier raised by TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee.    “Assam and Bengal are clear cases of the election being stolen by the BJP with the support of the EC,” he said.    Assam and Bengal are clear cases of the election being stolen by the BJP with the support of the EC.    We agree with Mamata ji. More than 100 seats were stolen in Bengal.    We have seen this playbook before:  Madhya Pradesh.  Haryana.  Maharashtra.  Lok Sabha 2024 etc    चुनाव चोरी,…  — Rahul Gandhi (@RahulGandhi) May 4, 2026      Backing Banerjee’s allegations of large-scale seat losses, he added, “We agree with Mamata ji. More than 100 seats were stolen in Bengal.”    Extending his criticism beyond the two eastern states, Gandhi claimed the alleged pattern was not isolated and suggested it had repeated across multiple electoral contests in recent years.    “We have seen this playbook before: Madhya Pradesh, Haryana, Maharashtra, Lok Sabha 2024 etc,” he said.    In a final remark, he intensified his attack on institutions, writing, “Election theft, institutional theft — what more is left?”    Meanwhile, according to Congress leader Jairam Ramesh, Gandhi also held a series of phone conversations with key political leaders following the announcement of results across states.    In a post on X, Ramesh said, “This evening, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi spoke to Mamata Banerjee-ji and Thiru MK Stalin about the election results. He also congratulated the President of the TVK Thiru Vijay on the party's performance.”    Ramesh also highlighted the Congress-led United Democratic Front’s strong performance in Kerala, calling it a “massive majority” mandate and a vote of confidence from the electorate.    “The Indian National Congress extends heartfelt thanks to the people of Kerala for giving the UDF the opportunity to serve with a massive majority. We recognize our responsibility and will honour the trust placed in us,” he said.    However, he acknowledged that the party’s performance in other regions fell short of expectations, while maintaining that the Congress remains committed to its ideological fight.    “Apart from Keralam, the other results that have come in fall short of our expectations. But we are neither discouraged nor disheartened. We are fighting a battle of ideologies. The path of fighting for democracy and truth against authoritarianism and lies is always long and arduous. However, we will continue to move forward with resolve and steadfast determination,” he said.    Ramesh further said that a detailed review of the election results would be conducted soon and confirmed that the process of deploying party observers to Kerala had already begun.    Counting for the 2026 Assembly elections began at 8 am across 823 constituencies in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Assam, and the Union Territory of Puducherry, beginning with postal ballots followed by Electronic Voting Machine counting from 8:30 am, with results updated in real time on the ECINET platform and the Election Commission’s official portal.

articles.description: In a post on X, hours after counting showed BJP crossing the 200-mark in Bengal, Kugelman noted that BJP has defeated on its biggest rivals in India, referring to the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress.
articles.body: US-based geopolitical expert Michael Kugelman on Monday described BJP's resounding victory in West Bengal as a &quot;massive political earthquake&quot;, adding that it's one of the largest to hit India in quite some time.    In a post on X, hours after counting showed BJP crossing the 200-mark in Bengal, Kugelman noted that BJP has defeated on its biggest rivals in India, referring to the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress.    &quot;The BJP’s likely victory in West Bengal is a massive political earthquake-one of the largest to hit India in quite some time. It has defeated one of its biggest rivals, who has run WB for 15 years, and it will hold power for the first time in India’s 4th most populous state,&quot; he said.    The BJP’s likely victory in West Bengal is a massive political earthquake-one of the largest to hit India in quite some time.  It has defeated one of its biggest rivals, who has run WB for 15 years, and it will hold power for the first time in India’s 4th most populous state.  — Michael Kugelman (@MichaelKugelman) May 4, 2026      BJP has scripted history after wresting West Bengal from Mamata's TMC with a landslide performance. The party is set to win over 200 seats in the 294-member assembly at a vote share of over 45%. The TMC is set to win over 75 seats, as per the latest counting trends.    In 2021, BJP improved its seat tally to 77 from 3 in 2016 in a remarkable surge but failed to dent Mamata's TMC which scripted a landslide victory after winning 211 seats.    The decisive performance by the party dealt a big blow to TMC, which had retained its iron grip on the state for the last 15 years after ousting the Left government in 2011.    West Bengal was seen as the final frontier for the BJP in the northern region with the party launching an all-out campaign over the last few weeks to wrest control from Mamata and bring in &quot;poriborton&quot; (change) in the state. Both PM Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah led BJP's campaign in the state and addressed multiple rallies, pitching itself as the much-needed alternative to the TMC, which the saffron party accused of fostering “gundagardi” and abetting infiltration.

articles.title: From confidence to collapse: Mamata Banerjee's fortress in Bhabanipur crashes as BJP sweeps Bengal
articles.snippet: Suvendu Adhikari dealt a crushing blow to Mamata Banerjee by defeating the TMC supremo in her home constituency, Bhabanipur, by 15,114 votes.
articles.author: Raajnandini Mukherjee
articles.description: Suvendu Adhikari dealt a crushing blow to Mamata Banerjee by defeating the TMC supremo in her home constituency, Bhabanipur, by 15,114 votes.
articles.body: As the counting of votes started on May 4, West Bengal Chief Minister and TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee put on a brave face, asked her party cadres not to lose hope and stay put at the counting centres till the votes were finally tallied and the winner declared.    Banerjee also said how the Election Commission was purposely withholding the results of some 70 seats where the TMC was projected to win to create a false narrative that the BJP was winning and pull down the morale of the TMC workers. She was confident that the tables would turn in her party's favour by sunset.    However, by evening, the TMC supremo looked embittered. While speaking to reporters, Banerjee said BJP has looted more than 100 seats with the help of the Election Commission. She admitted that the BJP was winning, calling it's victory in Bengal 'immoral.'    #WATCH | West Bengal CM &amp;amp; TMC chairperson Mamata Banerjee says, &quot;From 3 pm onwards, they have been beating us. I was hit. CCTV was switched off. None of our agents was allowed inside (the counting centre). The DO assured me our agents would be allowed, but after that, he was not… pic.twitter.com/vzZQvjqLOV  — ANI (@ANI) May 4, 2026      Her disappointment was even more marked as she walked out of the counting centre at the Sakhawat Memorial Girls' School amid chants of 'Ghotalabaaz Mamata' by BJP supporters.      #WATCH | Bhowanipore | BJP supporters chanted &quot;Ghotalabaaz Mamata dur hato&quot; as West Bengal CM &amp;amp; TMC chairperson exited from the Bhowanipore counting centre pic.twitter.com/urLW20KMFx    — ANI (@ANI) May 4, 2026          In a major political upset in West Bengal, Suvendu Adhikari dealt a crushing blow to Mamata Banerjee by defeating the TMC supremo in her home constituency, Bhabanipur, by 15,114 votes after 20 rounds of counting.    According to the final counting figures, Adhikari secured a vote share of 67,239 votes firmly outpacing Banerjee, who managed to secure 56,245 votes despite a fierce battle to hold on to one of her strongest political bastions.    The victory carries added political significance as this is not the first time Adhikari has emerged victorious against Banerjee. In the 2021 West Bengal Legislative Assembly election, the BJP leader had defeated Banerjee in Nandigram, one of the most high-profile contests of the election.    Even though Mamata lost Nandigram to Adhikari by a narrow margin, her party had already secured the mandate, winning over 200 seats in the 2021 Assembly elections, allowing her to be sworn in as Chief Minister for a third term.    Under the Constitution, a Chief Minister can take oath even if not an MLA at that moment, but must get elected to the assembly within six months. She later entered the assembly after winning the Bhabanipur bypoll.    Adhikari’s latest victory in Bhabanipur is now being seen as a significant symbolic and political setback for the TMC leadership.    The BJP clinched a decisive victory in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections, delivering a sweeping mandate and reshaping the state’s political landscape.

articles.title: Rajinikanth congratulates Vijay on TVK’s performance in Tamil Nadu election: 'Resounding victory'
articles.snippet: Apart from Rajinikanth and Dhanush, Vijay was also  congratulated by Telugu actor Chiranjeevi and his son Ram Charan.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: Apart from Rajinikanth and Dhanush, Vijay was also  congratulated by Telugu actor Chiranjeevi and his son Ram Charan.
articles.body: Actor-turned-politician Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) has registered a historic breakthrough in the Tamil Nadu Assembly Elections 2026, marking a significant entry for the party in state politics. Following the results, actor Rajinikanth congratulated Vijay, praising the mandate.    &quot;My congratulations to Thiru Vijay, President of the victorious Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam, and to the members of his party, on their resounding victory in the recently concluded Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly elections. @TVKVijayHQ,&quot;  said Rajinikanth in a post on X.    நடந்து முடிந்த தமிழக சட்டமன்றத் தேர்தலில் பெரும் வெற்றி பெற்ற தமிழக வெற்றிக் கழகத் தலைவர் திரு விஜய் அவர்களுக்கும், அவர் கட்சியினருக்கும் என்னுடைய வாழ்த்துகள். @TVKVijayHQ  — Rajinikanth (@rajinikanth) May 4, 2026      Dhanush also conveyed his heartfelt congratulations to Vijay. Apart from Rajinikanth and Dhanush, Vijay was also  congratulated by Telugu megastar Chiranjeevi and his son Ram Charan. Chiranjeevi praised Vijay’s well-earned victory, expressing hope that he would continue to inspire and lead with unwavering commitment, while Ram Charan highlighted Vijay’s deep connect with the people, which he said played a key role in his historic win in Tamil Nadu.    Tamil Nadu, long regarded as the stronghold of Dravidian politics for over five decades and traditionally shaped by a bipolar contest between the DMK and AIADMK, appears to be witnessing a political shift. Actor-turned-politician Vijay, who entered electoral politics with his party TVK, is now on course to emerge as the single-largest party, signalling a potential realignment in the state’s political landscape.    Vijay clinched victory from the Perambur constituency on Monday, defeating DMK candidate R D Shekar by a margin of 53,715 votes.    Congress leader Rahul Gandhi  also spoke with Vijay on Monday to congratulate him.  Gandhi noted that the election results signal the increasing influence of young voices in politics, stressing that this shift cannot be overlooked.    In a post on X, Gandhi said, &quot;I spoke to Thiru Vijay and congratulated him on TVK's spectacular result. This mandate reflects the rising voice of youth, which cannot, and will not, be ignored. I reiterate that the Congress party will continue to protect and serve the people of Tamil Nadu and Puducherry.&quot;

articles.title: 'Next  ...': BJP outlines 2027 election priority in prophetic X post
articles.snippet: BJP had made the exact same post for West Bengal on November 14 after the NDA won the Bihar elections last year.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: BJP had made the exact same post for West Bengal on November 14 after the NDA won the Bihar elections last year.
articles.body: The BJP on Monday outlined its priority just hours after winning the assembly elections in West Bengal with a prophetic post on X.    In a post on X, the BJP's Punjab handle wrote &quot;Next Punjab&quot; with an emoji of a lotus, indicating that the party has set its eyes on the state which will go to polls in the first half of 2027.    Interestingly, BJP had made the exact same post for West Bengal on November 14 after the NDA won the Bihar elections last year.    Next Punjab 🪷 https://t.co/UbHFK8VOCx  — BJP PUNJAB (@BJP4Punjab) May 4, 2026      The West Bengal handle of BJP had posted: &quot;Next West Bengal&quot; along with the lotus image.    BJP has already set its eyes on assembly elections in states like Uttar Pradesh and Punjab next year after dominating the last few state polls.    Last month, BJP dealt a heavy blow to the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) in Punjab after seven Rajya Sabha members belonging to the Arvind Kejriwal-led outfit joined hands with the saffron party. Six of these seven MPs, including Raghav Chadha, were elected from Punjab.    The switch, seen as a political coup de grâce on AAP, has set up a keen clash in Punjab next year where BJP is hoping to make gains and wrest from AAP.

articles.title: Kerala election results: Here's the final tally as per EC data
articles.snippet: The UDF has collectively won 97 seats while the LDF has won 35. The BJP has also made decent gains, winning 3 seats in this election after drawing a blank in 2021.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: The UDF has collectively won 97 seats while the LDF has won 35. The BJP has also made decent gains, winning 3 seats in this election after drawing a blank in 2021.
articles.body: The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) scripted a decisive victory in Kerala after winning 97 out of the 140 seats in the state, sweeping aside the ruling Left Democratic Front led by CPM.    As per the Election Commission data, after the conclusion of counting, the UDF has collectively won 97 seats while the LDF has won 35. The BJP has also made decent gains, winning 3 seats in this election after drawing a blank in 2021.    A party-wise breakdown shows that Congress won 63 seats with a vote share of nearly 29%. It is followed by Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) which won 22 seats, Kerala Congress (7), Revolutionary Socialist Party (3), Revolutionary Marxist Party of India (1) and Kerala Congress (Jacob) (1).        On the other end, CPM won 26 seats with a vote share of nearly 22%. It was followed by Communist Party of India (8) and Rashtriya Janata Dal (1). The other parties in the alliance failed to win any seat.    Notably, the BJP won 3 seats with a sizeable vote share of 11.42%.    In the 2021 elections, the LDF had retained power by winning 99 seats in the state.    The victory of UDF marks a return for Congress in Kerala after a gap of 10 years. Traditionally, the state has a history of revolving door politics, with voters generally voting out the incumbent.
