articles.title: Upset in Mamata bastion: Suvendu Adhikari leads TMC supremo in tight Bhabanipur battle, leads by 6,235...
articles.snippet: After 16 of the scheduled 20 rounds, Adhikari was ahead by 563 votes, polling 53,932 votes against Banerjee’s 53,369, according to ECI data
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: After 16 of the scheduled 20 rounds, Adhikari was ahead by 563 votes, polling 53,932 votes against Banerjee’s 53,369, according to ECI data
articles.body: A tight contest is underway in Bhabanipur Assembly constituency, with BJP's Suvendu Adhikari holding a narrow lead over TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee as counting progresses in the 2026 Assembly elections.    After 16 of the scheduled 20 rounds, Adhikari was ahead by 563 votes, polling 53,932 votes against Banerjee’s 53,369, according to data from the Election Commission of India.    The high-stakes contest has witnessed dramatic swings through the day. Banerjee had initially built a commanding lead of over 17,000 votes by the end of the seventh round, securing 32,822 votes against Adhikari’s 15,451. However, her advantage steadily narrowed in subsequent rounds.    Her lead dropped to 15,494 votes after the eighth round, fell to 12,131 by the 10th, and further reduced to 7,184 after 12 rounds. By the 14th round, the margin had shrunk sharply to 3,830 votes, before Adhikari edged ahead in the later stages.    The early rounds had already hinted at a fluctuating battle. Banerjee led in the first round, Adhikari briefly overtook in the second, and the chief minister regained and expanded her lead in the following rounds before the trend reversed.    Bhabanipur, long considered a stronghold of the ruling Trinamool Congress, has emerged as one of the most closely watched seats in the state.    The counting centre at Sakhawat Memorial Government Girls’ High School witnessed intense activity, with both leaders present. Banerjee arrived in the afternoon amid allegations by her party that one of its counting agents had been forced out, while Adhikari was already inside.    Emerging from the centre, Banerjee questioned the credibility of the process. “Do you think this is a victory? It is an immoral victory. More than 100 seats have been looted. The Election Commission is the BJP’s commission,” she alleged.    She further claimed irregularities, saying, “It is loot, loot, loot. We will bounce back,” and added that complaints had been raised with officials, including the Chief Electoral Officer. Banerjee also alleged that she was “pushed and berated” inside the counting centre.    There was no immediate response from the Election Commission or the Bharatiya Janata Party to the allegations.    With four rounds of counting still remaining, the Bhabanipur result remains too close to call, though momentum appears to have shifted towards Adhikari in the closing stages.

articles.title: Modi bharosa strengthened as BJP knocks down TMC in Bengal and ensures Stalin bites the dust in Tamil Nadu
articles.snippet: This electoral victory for the BJP in Bengal will go down in history as a refresh button on Modi Bharosa.
articles.author: Amitabh Sinha
articles.description: This electoral victory for the BJP in Bengal will go down in history as a refresh button on Modi Bharosa.
articles.body: This is indeed historic. This is unbelievable. This electoral victory for the BJP in Bengal will go down in history as a refresh button on Modi Bharosa. The defeat of Trinamool Congress and DMK led by Stalin has made it loud and clear that voters are fed up with corruption and family politics.    The BJP high command was always aware that the people want development, the youth want employment, and women, the silent voters of PM Modi, were in desperate need of empowerment. What this victory means for the BJP, the opposition will not be able to gauge. The towering leaders like Mamata Banerjee and Stalin relished in clashes with the Centre and agencies and failed to judge the pulse of the people. Now this is established beyond the fact that there is no one in the country of PM Modi's stature. Indeed, this is Modi Bharosa that the BJP has won three consecutive elections under PM Modi. It seems now that the word anti-incumbency has vanished from the BJP's dictionary.    This win is historic for a leader who works round the clock for the development of the country. For PM Modi, the confidence the people of the country bestowed upon him in the 2014 Lok Sabha polls was again visible in the Bengal assembly elections. The victory in Bengal can be put in the same league. Mamata Banerjee, who fought against left violence, continued to rule with the same violent system. She failed to understand that the people who voted for her wanted change in the system. To understand the mood of the voters in Gen Z's words, it would be apt to write that a refresh button has been pushed on Modi Bharosa in these polls, which, in turn, helps PM Modi take his decisions more confidently and implement his schemes more vehemently to realise the dreams of Viksit Bharat in 2047.    It's almost impossible to fulfil the voters' expectations.    After 15 years of rule, Mamata Banerjee was identified with violence unleashed by her system, Bangladeshi infiltration, and a changing demographic profile, while on the other hand, DMK supremo Stalin began singing the same tune by opening a front against the Modi govt and central agencies. What they failed to understand was that to fight against anti-incumbency, they had to win the confidence of the people.    That's why in Bengal, people saw the alternative in the BJP, while in Tamil Nadu, the voters put their bet on Tamil Superstar Vijay-led TVK party instead of DMK and AIADMK. The voters have ensured that the power doesn't go into the hands of DMK. After MGR and Jaya Lalitha, stars like Rajnikant and Kamal Hasan could not face the might of DMK and AIADMK, but Vijay has made it possible. He was charged with the death of innocent people due to the rush in his rally, and even the BJP pushed hard to make a deal for an alliance. But this didn't materialise. But higher-ups in the BJP insisted that something unexpected is bound to happen in Tamil Nadu.    Now let's talk about the victory of the BJP in Bengal. In the 2021 assembly polls in the state, the BJP fought tooth and nail in the first four phases and won 77 seats. It was around 7-phase polls, and after the 4th phase, Corona was at its peak, and the BJP's all plans went haywire. Neither PM Modi could campaign in the last 3 phases, nor were the workers placed at booths and strategic locations.    In the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, the BJP won only 8 seats, but led in more than 90 assembly seats. Their vote share increased tremendously.  Therefore, when the BJP high command started planning for the 2026 polls, the priority was to strike at the base of violence and ensure that the voters come out in higher numbers.    Last month, during the budget session, one of the top leaders involved rightly pointed out to me, &quot;Nikal Gaye to Nikal Jayenge,&quot; meaning if people come out to vote, the BJP will come out victorious. The massive deployment of CAPF, the Central Election Commission's proactive approach despite all-out attack by the Trinamool leadership and other opposition leaders ensured that goons remained underground and behind bars.    The BJP ensured that the local leadership of Bengal was given prominence. The leaders from Delhi became backroom boys managing elections. This nailed the TMC narrative of the BJP neglecting Bengali leadership. Apart from rallies and road shows, three visuals of Prime Minister Modi were also considered to be a game-changer. The first was of PM enjoying Jhalmuri with common people at a local market made it possible for the BJP to negate Mamata's vision of buying vegetables. The second visual was of PM Modi enjoying a boat ride in the Hooghly river and interacting with the boatmen community and common people at the ghat, and thirdly, for a football-loving state like Bengal, the visuals of PM Modi playing football with kids at Gangtok made an impact not only on football fans but Gen Z as well.    Even in Assam, the BJP won for the third consecutive time, and that too due to the PM Modi government's policies being implemented successfully on the ground, and CM Hemanta Biswa Sarma ensured that the government remained on the ground to remove anti-incumbency. Now, with Bengal in firm grip and Tamil Nadu out of bounds for the DMK for the next five years, the BJP high command has now full time to focus on Karnataka and Kerala.    PM Modi now has one regret that amendments to the women's reservation bill to ensure 1/3rd representation for women in Lok Sabha in the 2029 polls were not passed in the parliament. These polls have proved that Modi Bharosa is intact among the voters across the country.

articles.title: By winning West Bengal, BJP has made whole of North East more safe: Himanta Biswa Sarma
articles.snippet: Sarma secured a decisive victory in Jalukbari, winning the seat with 89,562 votes.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: Sarma secured a decisive victory in Jalukbari, winning the seat with 89,562 votes.
articles.body: As the counting of votes for the Assembly elections was underway on Monday, Assam Chief Minister and BJP leader Himanta Biswa Sharma congratulated the party's decisive victory in Assam and West Bengal.    Speaking to reporters after the BJP's victory in Assam, Sarma said, &quot;Whatever I say is told to me by Ma Khamakhya. When I went to Siliguri for an election rally, I randomly said BJP will win 100 seats in Assam and over 200 in West Bengal. Ma Khamakhya made me say it.&quot;    &quot;By securing a decisive victory in West Bengal, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah will be able to take necessary steps to enhance the safety and security of the nation...When I drive out someone from Assam, he/she gets the scope again to enter the country via West Bengal,&quot; said the Assam CM.    #WATCH | Guwahati | Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma says,&quot; I thank both the PM and Union Home Minister, by winning West Bengal, we have made the whole of North East more safe.&quot; pic.twitter.com/3fX3xlanWQ  — ANI (@ANI) May 4, 2026      &quot;Now, from Bengal to Mizoram, we have our government. Under the vision of Home Minister Amit Shah, if the Chief Ministers of five states---Assam, Mizoram, Meghalaya, Tripura, West Bengal--- work together, the stretch from the Chicken's neck (Siliguri) to the whole of northeast India will be secure,&quot; said Sarma.    Stating that Home Minister Amit Shah did not focus on West Bengal to make BJP win but to make the whole country win, Sarma said, &quot;I thank both Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. By winning West Bengal, we have made the whole of North East more safe.&quot;    With the conclusion of counting in Jalukbari, Sarma secured a decisive victory, winning the seat with 89,562 votes and extending his winning streak in the constituency.    The result reinforces Jalukbari’s position as a BJP stronghold and underlines Sarma’s continued political dominance in Assam. The victory marks Sarma's sixth consecutive win from the seat and paves the way for his fourth consecutive term as CM.    In West Bengal, the election trends show that the BJP has won 58 seats and is leading in 146 other assembly constituencies. The West Bengal Legislative Assembly has 294 seats and the majority mark is 147.    &amp;nbsp;

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election results 2026: Why MK Stalin's Kolathur loss carries deeper political weight |...
articles.snippet: In the 2026 election, Stalin was defeated in Kolathur by Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam’s (TVK) VS Babu, a former associate, by a margin of 8795 votes.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: In the 2026 election, Stalin was defeated in Kolathur by Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam’s (TVK) VS Babu, a former associate, by a margin of 8795 votes.
articles.body: This is not the first electoral defeat for MK Stalin, but the 2026 result is being viewed differently. Earlier losses came at moments shaped by sweeping political currents. This time, however, the defeat arrives when he is at the peak of his leadership as president of the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK).    In the 2026 election, Stalin was defeated in Kolathur by Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam’s (TVK) VS Babu, a former associate, by a margin of 8795 votes. The constituency had, until now, been a stronghold he had carefully built over the years. That context is what makes the loss more striking.    Earlier defeats shaped by larger waves    Stalin’s first electoral defeat came in 1984 from Chennai’s Thousand Lights constituency. At the time, he was a 31-year-old youth wing secretary entering politics during a turbulent phase. The verdict, as described, was not personal but situational.    The election unfolded amid extraordinary circumstances. The assassination of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi triggered a nationwide sympathy wave, while then Chief Minister MG Ramachandran (MGR)’s illness added another emotional dimension in Tamil Nadu.    The AIADMK-Congress alliance swept the polls decisively, leaving the DMK with just 24 seats out of 170 contested. Stalin lost, but the conditions were stacked against him.    He returned in 1989 to win from the same constituency and went on to secure multiple victories in subsequent elections.    The 1991 loss and political upheaval    His next major defeat came in 1991, again in Thousand Lights. The political climate had shifted dramatically following the assassination of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi. The election saw a strong anti-DMK wave.    Stalin lost to KA Krishnaswamy of the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) by 16,981 votes. The result reflected a broader electoral shift rather than a constituency-specific rejection. The DMK was reduced to a marginal presence as the AIADMK-Congress alliance swept the state.    Reinvention through Kolathur    In 2011, Stalin made a strategic move by shifting from Thousand Lights to Kolathur. It was described as “a bold political reset,” and it paid off at the individual level.    Even as the DMK faced a major defeat statewide, winning only 23 seats amid the fallout of the 2G spectrum controversy -- Stalin retained Kolathur. His choice of constituency, rooted in a working-class urban base, proved effective.    He strengthened this position over time. In 2016, he won with a significant margin, and by 2021, Kolathur had become a fortress, delivering him over 60% vote share and a massive lead.    Why 2026 is different    The 2026 defeat breaks that trajectory. Unlike 1984 or 1991, there is no singular statewide emotional wave or extraordinary external factor cited as the primary cause. Instead, the loss comes in a constituency he had consolidated over a decade.    This makes the result politically symbolic. It suggests a shift not just in electoral outcomes but in voter behaviour within areas once considered secure.    Several senior DMK leaders -- including Thangam Thennarasu, TRB Rajaa, EV Velu, KN Nehru, and Ma. Subramanian -- were also trailing, indicating broader electoral challenges for the party. He was among 14 DMK ministers who were trailing in their respective constituencies even after the third round of counting.    A generational inflection point    The larger narrative surrounding the result ties into a changing political landscape in Tamil Nadu. The rise of new players like TVK and the defeat of an established leader in his stronghold point toward a potential transition phase.    Stalin’s earlier losses were shaped by extraordinary political tides. This one, however, appears rooted in shifting ground realities.

articles.title: West Bengal Election Results: Biggest wins see margins soar up to 90,000 votes, check details
articles.snippet: At the top of the chart is Dabgram‑Phulbari, where the All India Trinamool Congress is trailing with a gap of staggering 90,188 votes. TMC won 211 seats in 2016 elections while in 2021 it was reduced to just 22.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: At the top of the chart is Dabgram‑Phulbari, where the All India Trinamool Congress is trailing with a gap of staggering 90,188 votes. TMC won 211 seats in 2016 elections while in 2021 it was reduced to just 22.
articles.body: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) moved toward a landslide victory in the West Bengal Assembly elections on Monday, leading in 188 seats as counting progressed. As per the latest Election Commission of India (ECI) data available, the party has officially been declared the winner in 12 seats.    Here's a list of seats in West Bengal where major parties were not just defeated, but crushed by margins running from 45,000 to over 90,000 votes.    Dabgram‑Phulbari    At the top of the chart is Dabgram‑Phulbari, where the All India Trinamool Congress is trailing with a gap of staggering 90,188 votes. TMC won 211 seats in 2016 elections while in 2021 it was reduced to just 22.    TMC's Abdul Khaleque Molla won the Metiaburuz seat crushing Bharatiya Janata Party candidate by more than 87,879 votes, marking one of the widest margins for the BJP in the state.    These two numbers alone show how both national and regional heavyweights can get wiped out when local equations go wrong.    North Bengal    Several northern seats in the list highlight heavy defeats for both sides.    Matigara‑Naxalbari and Siliguri see Trinamool as the trailing party with margins of 74,427 and 61,994 votes respectively as BJP leads suggesting the party’s weaknesses in some urban and tea‑belt segments even as it dominates the south.    On the other hand, BJP is trailing by 71,775 votes in Goalpokhar and by over 52,000 in Malatipur and Harischandrapur—constituencies where the party has struggled to convert its broader North Bengal advantage into a consistent sweep.    South Bengal    In Kultali, for instance, BJP is trailing by 58,545 votes, while in Bhagabangola the Communist Party candidate is behind by 56,407 votes—evidence of how far the Left has slipped in many rural Muslim‑majority pockets.    Trinamool’s rivals face steep deficits in seats like Bankura, Krishnanagar Uttar, Goghat, Raiganj, Maynaguri and Maldaha, where the trailing party is TMC’s main opponent and the margin ranges from about 44,800 to 48,200 votes.    These are the kinds of margins that make a seat look “safe” for the winner in the short term, but also risk breeding complacency.    Congress and smaller parties    In Sujapur, the Indian National Congress appears as the trailing party with a hefty 60,287‑vote gap—one of the largest defeats listed for any national party in this snapshot.    Canning Purba stands out for the All India Secular Front, where it trails by 49,973 votes, underlining how hard it is for smaller outfits to break through beyond a few pockets of influence.    What 40–90k margins say about Bengal’s battlefield    Across the 27 constituencies captured in this sheet, trailing parties are behind by anywhere between roughly 44,800 and 90,000 votes.    For Trinamool, the warning lights blink in places like Dabgram‑Phulbari, Siliguri and Matigara‑Naxalbari; for BJP, the red zones include Metiaburuz, Goalpokhar and a string of Malda and Murshidabad seats; for Congress and the Left, the figures simply confirm how few deep pockets they have left.    For strategists in every camp, these are the “no‑contest” seats that rarely get attention on counting day—but they tell a sharper story about where each party’s narrative collapses completely, and where any future revival will be hardest to script.

articles.title: BJP makes inroads into Muslim belts, setback for TMC: How Muslim-majority seats voted in West Bengal
articles.snippet: Latest trends indicate that TMC has ceded 9 Muslim seats compared to the 2021 Assembly elections while BJP has added 4 such seats, signaling a shift in voting patterns.
articles.author: Sonalee Borgohain
articles.description: Latest trends indicate that TMC has ceded 9 Muslim seats compared to the 2021 Assembly elections while BJP has added 4 such seats, signaling a shift in voting patterns.
articles.body: In a massive win for BJP, the party has conveniently surged past the majority mark in West Bengal dealing a major blow to the ruling Trinamool Congress (TMC). With leads in over 200 seats, the saffron party appears set to upend the state's political landscape, long dominated by TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee.    Not only has the BJP managed to woo women voters, it is also making inroads into Muslim-dominated areas in West Bengal. Latest trends indicate that TMC has ceded 9 Muslim seats compared to the 2021 Assembly elections while BJP has added 4 such seats, signaling a shift in voting patterns.    According to Suvendu Adhikari, who is seen as a possible CM face for the BJP, signs of a split in the Muslim vote are especially evident in Malda, Murshidabad and North Dinajpur. &quot;In South Bengal and Cooch Behar, Muslims are still initially leaning more towards the TMC, but the kind of 90–95% consolidation seen in 2021 and 2024 is no longer there. There are visible cracks in that support base,&quot; he said.    In the previous Assembly lections, the BJP drew a blank in Muslim-majority areas despite securing over 21.6% of Muslim vote across the state. In contrast, the TMC dominated such constituencies in 2021, particularly in Murshidabad - where Muslims make up a significant population. The Mamata-led party swept 43 of 44 Muslim seats in the 2021 Assembly elections. According to the latest update, the Congress, which put up a dismal show in West Bengal this election, managed to win two of 44 Muslim-majority seats.    Muslim-dominated districts like Murshidabad, Malda, and Uttar Dinajpur play a crucial role in West Bengal elections. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise recorded more than 4.5 lakh deletions in Murshidabad and around 2.3 lakh in Malda, while additions in several Muslim-dominated constituencies were relatively modest.    While BJP is far ahead of TMC in the state, Mamata Banerjee is maintaining a strong edge in her Bhabanipur stronghold. After eight rounds of counting, she is ahead by over 5,000 votes against her nearest rival Suvendu Adhikari, offering the TMC some early relief in this high-profile contest.    Adhikari claims there's Hindu consolidation. &quot;... The way Muslims vote for TMC, they have not done that this time. Some votes have gone to the pro-Muslim party. BJP has also got some in small amounts. I was not expecting such a good performance in the Muslim booth in Nandigram ... The guarantee given by PM Modi to build Bengal under his leadership has been in his favour,&quot; he said.    In the 2011 Assembly elections, widespread discontent over the Left Front's land acquisition policies triggered a consolidation of Muslim votes in favour of change, helping TMC bring an end to 34 years of Left rule.

articles.title: VGRC Surat: Driving industrial &amp; economic transformation in south Gujarat
articles.snippet: The government signed 2,792 MoUs worth Rs 3,53,306 crore during the two-day conference, which are expected to generate 2.82 lakh direct employment opportunities in the coming years.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: The government signed 2,792 MoUs worth Rs 3,53,306 crore during the two-day conference, which are expected to generate 2.82 lakh direct employment opportunities in the coming years.
articles.body: The Vibrant Gujarat Regional Conferences have emerged as an innovative initiative, expanding the reach and impact of the successful Vibrant Gujarat Global Summit—a pathbreaking initiative pioneered under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his tenure as Chief Minister of Gujarat.    Over the years, the summit has evolved into one of the most reputed global platforms for business networking, knowledge sharing, and strategic partnerships focused on inclusive growth and sustainable development.    Continuing the success of the first two editions held in Mehsana and Rajkot, the Surat chapter representing South Gujarat also witnessed tremendous success. The government signed 2,792 MoUs worth Rs 3,53,306 crore during the two-day conference, which are expected to generate 2.82 lakh direct employment opportunities in the coming years.    Chief Minister Shri Bhupendra Patel inaugurated the third Vibrant Gujarat Regional Conference (VGRC) in Surat and stated that the initiative is inspired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision to ensure that no region of the state is left behind and that each district’s potential is showcased on a global platform. He added that the South Gujarat VGRC will accelerate industrial development across Surat, Tapi, Navsari, Valsad, Dang, and Bharuch.    A grand exhibition reflecting holistic development across industrial growth, green energy, agriculture, and the service sector was inaugurated at AURO University by the Chief Minister. The five-day exhibition was divided into three sections: industrial and manufacturing, green energy and sustainable development and agriculture, food processing, and services—featuring innovative products, technologies, machinery, startup solutions, and government schemes.    Referring to the success of previous VGRCs in North Gujarat and Saurashtra-Kutch, the Chief Minister emphasized that such regional conferences are key to building a developed Gujarat and contributing to the vision of a developed India through inclusive growth.    A significant panel discussion on “Strategies to achieve self-reliance through import substitution in the fertilizer sector” highlighted the need to boost domestic production of urea, DAP, and complex fertilizers. It also emphasized promoting alternatives such as nano urea, organic fertilizers, and bio-fertilizers to reduce import dependence.    On the theme “The Next Era of Nuclear Energy,” experts from industry, policy, and technology sectors discussed challenges such as high capital costs, financing constraints, waste management, and public acceptance. The session also outlined pathways to strengthen India’s energy security and achieve the vision of Developed India@2047.    A seminar on “Transforming Chemicals and Petrochemicals in Gujarat” focused on future growth, planning, emerging opportunities, and strategic priorities for the sector. Addressing a seminar on “Rural, Tribal and Wedding Tourism,” Minister Shri Jayrambhai Gamit highlighted the role of tourism in generating rural employment and outlined initiatives undertaken by the state government, including the development of destinations such as Saputara.    The Chief Minister also announced the establishment of eight new “Smart GIDC” industrial estates across South Gujarat—two in Surat, three in Bharuch, and one each in Valsad, Tapi, and Navsari—covering a total area of 5,380 acres.    Deputy Chief Minister Shri Harsh Sanghavi extended greetings on Gujarat Foundation Day and stated that the VGRC will provide fresh momentum to the development of Surat and South Gujarat. He added that such regional conferences are being held across four zones to expand the reach of Vibrant Gujarat. The event was attended by international dignitaries, industry leaders, government officials, and entrepreneurs from sectors such as diamonds, textiles, and manufacturing. In a meeting with the  Chief Minister, Japan’s Ambassador to India, Mr. Ono Keiichi, reaffirmed Japan’s commitment to strengthening economic collaboration with Gujarat, particularly in the semiconductor sector.    Singapore’s High Commissioner to India, Mr. Simon Wong, noted that Singapore’s investments in Gujarat have been steadily increasing, including significant participation in GIFT City. He expressed confidence that GIFT City will emerge as a hub for USD-INR bond issuance and highlighted opportunities in data centres, AI-driven fintech, and data localization. He added that Singapore is keen to collaborate with India as it emerges as a major data and financial hub.    During a meeting with the Chief Minister, Rwanda’s High Commissioner to India, H.E. Ms. Jacqueline Mukangira, emphasized Rwanda’s importance as a partner country and discussed strengthening bilateral economic cooperation with Gujarat. On the occasion, Union Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri and Union Jal Shakti Minister Shri C.R. Patil also congratulated Gujarat for organizing regional summits.    Highlighting the role of women in economic growth, the panel discussion on “Nari Shakti in Surat: Viksit Surat for Viksit Bharat” showcased the transformative contribution of women across entrepreneurship, innovation, AI, digital ecosystems, and emerging sectors such as drone technology and defence.    In the run-up to the Vibrant Gujarat Global Summit 2027, the regional conferences stand as a testament to Gujarat’s decentralized growth strategy driving investment, fostering innovation, and accelerating the journey towards Viksit Bharat.

articles.title: BJP knocks on South's door: How party's performance in Kerala and Tamil Nadu compares to 2021 and why it...
articles.snippet: In Kerala, the BJP has made a modest but notable breakthrough. After failing to win a single seat in the 2021 Assembly elections, the party has now opened its account, bagging three seats.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: In Kerala, the BJP has made a modest but notable breakthrough. After failing to win a single seat in the 2021 Assembly elections, the party has now opened its account, bagging three seats.
articles.body: The Bharatiya Janata Party’s performance in southern states in the 2026 Assembly elections may not appear dramatic at first glance, but the numbers tell a story of gradual expansion. In regions where the party has historically struggled to gain ground, even incremental gains are politically significant and signal a deeper shift in voter behaviour.    In Kerala, the BJP has made a modest but notable breakthrough. After failing to win a single seat in the 2021 Assembly elections, the party has now opened its account, bagging three seats. While this is still far from a strong presence in the state, it marks an important psychological shift. Kerala has long been dominated by the Left Democratic Front and the United Democratic Front, leaving little room for a third force. Any foothold here helps the BJP position itself as a long-term contender rather than a marginal player.    In Tamil Nadu, the party’s performance reflects stability rather than expansion. The BJP had won four seats in the 2021 Assembly elections. This time, it is leading in three constituencies including Thalli, Udhagamandalam and Sattur. While the numbers have not surged, maintaining a presence in Tamil Nadu’s competitive political landscape is significant. The state has been dominated by regional parties like the DMK and AIADMK for decades, making it difficult for national parties to gain traction.    The BJP’s approach in the south has been gradual and layered. Instead of seeking immediate large-scale victories, the party has focused on building local networks, strengthening alliances and identifying winnable pockets. These incremental gains are crucial for long-term expansion. A seat here and there may not change the balance of power immediately, but they help the party establish a base, nurture local leadership and increase visibility.    Such gains also carry symbolic weight. Winning even a single seat in a state where the party previously had none sends a message of growing acceptance. It allows the BJP to project itself as a pan-India force, capable of competing beyond its traditional strongholds in the north and west.    &amp;nbsp;

articles.title: A win in Kerala, rout in Assam, below par performance in Tamil Nadu &amp; Bengal: How Congress fared in this...
articles.snippet: The loss in Assam will hurt the Congress the most as it was believed to be a 'real challenger' to the Himanta Biswa Sarma-led National Democratic Alliance.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: The loss in Assam will hurt the Congress the most as it was believed to be a 'real challenger' to the Himanta Biswa Sarma-led National Democratic Alliance.
articles.body: If the Congress were to critically analyse this round of state polls, held in four states --  kerala, Assam, West Bengal and Tamil Nadu, the grand old party will not have too much to write about except for its solitary win in Kerala.    What may be alarming for the grand old party is their complete decimation in states where it was expected to put up a decent fight. Barring Kerala, where the party has won in 30 seats and is leading in another 30, it has performed abysmally in the northeastern state of Assam where it is leading merely in 20 seats.    The loss in Assam will hurt the Congress the most as it was believed to be a 'real challenger' to the Himanta Biswa Sarma-led National Democratic Alliance.    Almost a year before the polls, the party had strategically announced Lok Sabha MP Gaurav Gogoi as the president of Pradesh Congress. Added to the 'strategic'  naming of Gogoi, Lok Sabha MP Priyanka Gandhi oversaw the ticket distribution process in the northeastern state.    Gaurav Gogoi has fallen short in Jorhat, Assam, finishing with 46,257 votes as the result was declared. BJP candidate Hitendra Nath Goswami, the sitting legislator from the constituency, held off the challenge to win the seat with 69,439 votes, a margin of 23,182.    Congress performance in Assam:     The grand old party is leading on 20 seats in the northeastern state, a big climbdown from its performance in 2016 and 2021. The party faced multiple setbacks leading upto the polls where many of its senior leaders switched sides to BJP.  The Assam results have not only weakened Congress as a whole but have also placed its state leadership under serious strain, with Gogoi losing from Jorhat.    Gaurav Gogoi’s campaign carried more than just political ambition. It also carried legacy. He is the son of the late Tarun Gogoi, Assam’s longest-serving Chief Minister and a towering figure in the state’s Congress history. After Tarun Gogoi’s death in 2020, the party entered the 2021 elections without a clear face, and suffered a major defeat.    Congress performance in West Bengal:    Congress remained on the margins in the West Bengal assembly election 2026, with limited seat impact despite a measurable vote base.    The Congress managed to secure just 2 seats as per the leads, while the CPI(M) is restricted to 1 seat, underlining how the contest stayed largely bipolar between the Trinamool Congress and the BJP. On the vote share front, Congress polled 3.25% (11,99,566 votes), while CPI(M) did slightly better with 4.24% (15,64,863 votes).    Even though both parties retained pockets of support, the numbers showed that this did not translate into seats at scale. The gap between vote share and seat conversion reflected a continued erosion of their electoral strength in the state, where they once dominated the political landscape. The final tally is yet to be released.    Congress performance in Tamil Nadu:     In the southern state of Tamil Nadu, the grand old party is leading in four seats and have won in two seats. In Tamil Nadu, the Congress has allied with the DMK.    The Congress’s performance so far suggests that it is struggling to translate alliance strength into electoral gains. With just 5 leads out of 28 contested seats, the party’s strike rate remains low compared to its allies. In a state where alliances often play a decisive role, such a gap highlights the difference between benefiting from a coalition and actually delivering wins.    &amp;nbsp;

articles.title: Baramati: Maharashtra Deputy CM Sunetra Pawar wins debut assembly election with record margin
articles.snippet: Riding the sympathy wave, Sunetra Pawar's victory margin has surpassed that of her late husband, who defeated BJP's Gopichand Padalkar by 1,65,265 votes in 2019.
articles.author: PTI
articles.description: Riding the sympathy wave, Sunetra Pawar's victory margin has surpassed that of her late husband, who defeated BJP's Gopichand Padalkar by 1,65,265 votes in 2019.
articles.body: Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister and NCP president, Sunetra Pawar, on Monday won the bypoll from the Baramati assembly seat with a margin of 2,18,034 votes, according to the figures shared by the Election Commission.    She secured 2,18,969 votes in the byelection necessitated by the death of her husband and then Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar.    The NCP claimed that Sunetra Pawar has set a new national record of the highest victory margin in the assembly elections, surpassing the previous record attributed to BJP's Sunil Kumar Sharma, who had won the Sahibabad segment by 2.14 lakh votes in 2022.    The other 22 candidates in the fray in Baramati together secured 4,837 votes.    Kiran Gujar, a close aide of the Pawar family, claimed Sunetra Pawar secured 98 per cent of the total votes polled.    The byelection was held on April 23 after the death of Baramati MLA Ajit Pawar in a plane crash on January 28.    Riding the sympathy wave, Sunetra Pawar's victory margin has surpassed that of her late husband, who defeated BJP's Gopichand Padalkar by 1,65,265 votes in 2019. In the 2024 elections, Ajit Pawar's victory margin was reduced to over 1 lakh votes.    A voter turnout of 58.27 per cent was recorded in the Baramati Assembly constituency on April 23.    In a post on X, Sunetra Pawar thanked the people of Baramati for the overwhelming mandate.    &quot;I sincerely thank the people of Baramati for electing me with an overwhelming mandate in the Baramati Assembly by-election. The trust, love, and support you have shown are of great importance to me,&quot; she stated.    She added that Ajit Pawar’s guidance and presence are deeply missed at this moment.    &quot;For me, this victory is not merely a political success but a true tribute to his work and his memory. His contribution to Maharashtra and Baramati, his strong connection with the people, and his vision for development continue to live in everyone's hearts.    &quot;His values and teachings give me the strength to move forward. I am fully aware that this victory brings with it the responsibility of carrying forward his dreams and legacy,&quot; she added.    Sunetra Pawar also thanked all NCP workers, office-bearers, and Mahayuti constituents- BJP and Shiv Sena- as well as the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi.    &quot;I remain committed to upholding the ideological legacy of Chhatrapati Shivaji, Shahu, Phule, and Ambedkar, and to walking on the path shown by respected Yashwantrao Chavan and Ajitdada. Let us work together for the development of Baramati, keeping youth, farmers, women, entrepreneurs, and every section of society at the centre,&quot; she added.    The NCP president has appealed to people not to take out victory processions, urging them to celebrate the win through work rather than festivities.    &quot;I assure you that I will never fall short of the trust you have placed in me and will always stand firmly with you in your joys and sorrows,&quot; she added.    NCP (SP) leader Rohit Pawar congratulated Sunetra Pawar on her spectacular win.    &quot;The victory is a real tribute and an expression of love for Ajitdada,&quot; he said.

articles.title: By-Poll Results Update: BJP wins Umreth, Rahuri, Koridang, and Dharmanagar; Congress retains Bagalkot,...
articles.snippet: Nagaland and Tripura had taken a significant lead in voter participation during the assembly by-elections on April 9, according to the data revealed by the Election Commission of India.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: Nagaland and Tripura had taken a significant lead in voter participation during the assembly by-elections on April 9, according to the data revealed by the Election Commission of India.
articles.body: Bharatiya Janata Party has swept bypolls in Gujarat Umreth, Maharashtra's Rahuri, Nagaland's Koridang and Tripura's Dharmanagar seats while Congress retained  Bagalkot, Davanagere South seats in Karnataka.    In Nagaland, BJP's Daochier I. Imchen won the by-election to the Koridang constituency, continuing the party's momentum in the northeastern state.    Meanwhile, in Tripura, BJP's Jahar Chakraborti clinched a win in the Assembly byelection to the Dharmanagar constituency.    Nagaland and Tripura had taken a significant lead in voter participation during the assembly by-elections on April 9, according to the data revealed by the Election Commission of India.    In Karnataka, Bagalkot and Davanagere South seats were retained by the ruling Indian National Congress. The elections, necessitated by the vacancies following the passing of sitting legislators, saw key contests between major national and regional parties.    In Gujarat's Umreth, BJP candidate Harshad Parmar won the bypoll defeating his nearest rival from Congress, Bhrugurajsinh Chauhan, by a margin of more than 30,000 votes.    In Rahuri, the Bharatiya Janata Party retained the assembly seat in Maharashtra after its candidate Akshay Kardile defeated Govind Mokate of the NCP (SP) by a margin of more than 1.12 lakh votes.    The bypoll to the constituency in Ahilyanagar district was necessitated due to the death of Kardile's father and sitting MLA Shivajirao Kardile.    As per data from the Election Commission of India, Kardile's secured 1,40,093 votes, while Mokate got 27,506 votes.    In Maharashtra Baramati, Sunetra Pawar, who heads the NCP, bagged more than 2 lakh votes at the time this report was published, taking a decisive lead over her 22 rivals, who could not even cross the 500-vote mark, according to the latest data on the Election Commission's website.    The byelection, held on April 23, was necessitated due to the death of the then Deputy CM and Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) head Ajit Pawar in a plane crash near Baramati airstrip in Pune district on January 28.    His wife Sunetra Pawar, contesting her first assembly poll, is poised for a huge win riding a sympathy wave, and given her family's strong hold on the constituency. No major political party has fielded candidates against her.

articles.title: No proposal to compensate oil marketing companies, says Govt
articles.snippet: According to rating agency ICRA, state-run OMCs are currently making negative marketing margins of around Rs 14 per litre on petrol and Rs 18 per litre on diesel at prevailing crude prices
articles.author: Arunima Bharadwaj
articles.description: According to rating agency ICRA, state-run OMCs are currently making negative marketing margins of around Rs 14 per litre on petrol and Rs 18 per litre on diesel at prevailing crude prices
articles.body: The government presently has no proposal to compensate state run oil marketing companies or provide financial support to them for losses being incurred in sales of auto fuels and LPG, according to a senior official in oil ministry.    “The government does not have any proposal that talks about supporting oil marketing companies,” Sujata Sharma, joint secretary, ministry of petroleum and natural gas said on May 4.  Sharma also said that there has been no increase in retail prices of petrol and diesel. “Our supplies have been impacted and there is tightness in the market,” she said.    According to rating agency ICRA, state-run OMCs are currently making negative marketing margins of around Rs 14 per litre on petrol and Rs 18 per litre on diesel at prevailing crude prices.  “Stable pump prices for auto fuels amid elevated crude oil prices are impacting the profitability of the oil marketing companies despite the recent reduction in excise duty.    With supplies of LPG disrupted from West Asia, international LPG prices have surged. While LPG production has been increased by the refining companies and cargoes procured from the US and Australia have addressed supply constraints to an extent, under-recoveries on domestic LPG remain high,” said Prashant Vasisht, Senior Vice President and Co-Group Head, Corporate Ratings, ICRA.    ICRA estimates LPG under-recoveries at around Rs 80,000 crore for FY27 if current trends persist. Commercial LPG prices have already been raised by around Rs 993 per cylinder.    Government sources told Moneycontrol that state-run fuel retailers may raise petrol and diesel prices in the coming days to offset mounting losses from selling fuel below cost, signalling a possible end to the prolonged price freeze despite Brent crude nearly doubling since the start of the war in West Asia.    The possible hike comes as global crude prices remain elevated, with Brent crude hovering around $108 per barrel. Retail petrol and diesel prices in India have largely remained unchanged since early April 2022, compressing marketing margins and increasing pressure on OMC balance sheets.

articles.title: Kerala voters' trust in us will guide UDF: Priyanka hails Cong win
articles.snippet: In a post on X, Gandhi said, "To all my brothers and sisters in Keralam, thank you for your faith and for your overwhelming support."
articles.author: PTI
articles.description: In a post on X, Gandhi said, &quot;To all my brothers and sisters in Keralam, thank you for your faith and for your overwhelming support.&quot;
articles.body: With the Congress-led UDF bagging a major win in the Kerala polls, Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on Monday thanked the people of the state for their overwhelming support and vowed to work diligently towards building a better future for them.    In a post on X, Gandhi said, &quot;To all my brothers and sisters in Keralam, thank you for your faith and for your overwhelming support. The trust you have placed in us will be the UDF’s guiding force as we work hard towards building a better future for each one of you.&quot; &quot;I sincerely hope that our gratitude to you will be evident each day of the next five years as we strive to fulfil our commitments to you with honesty and humility,&quot; she added.    നന്ദി കേരളം! ❤️    To all my brothers and sisters in Keralam, thank you for your faith and for your overwhelming support.    The trust you have placed in us will be the UDF’s guiding force as we work hard towards building a better future for each one of you.    I sincerely hope that…  — Priyanka Gandhi Vadra (@priyankagandhi) May 4, 2026      &quot;To my family in Wayanad, you have renewed your belief in the UDF with a resounding mandate – 7 out of 7 seats!! You now have 8 representatives working together towards the development of Wayanad! We will do all we can to live up to your expectations,&quot; the MP from Wayanad said.    &quot;To the workers and leaders of the UDF who worked day and night to take our message of a united and progressive Keralam to every household, my heartiest congratulations, best wishes and gratitude for your tireless efforts,&quot; Gandhi's post read.    According to the Election Commission website, the UDF was leading or had won in over 95 constituencies and appears poised to secure a comfortable majority in the 140-member House. articles.title: BJP makes solid gains in Kerala, set to win 3 seats in historic breakthrough
articles.snippet: For the first time in Kerala’s electoral history, the BJP is set to win three Assembly seats.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: For the first time in Kerala’s electoral history, the BJP is set to win three Assembly seats.
articles.body: In a notable shift in the 2026 Kerala Assembly elections, the Rajeev Chandrasekhar-led Bharatiya Janata Party has managed to open its account in the state, marking a significant milestone in a region where it has traditionally struggled.    For the first time in Kerala’s electoral history, the BJP is set to win three Assembly seats. Rajeev Chandrasekhar secured victory in Nemom in Thiruvananthapuram, while B. B. Gopakumar won from Chathannoor in Kollam district, and V. Muraleedharan emerged victorious in Kazhakkoottam. This comes after the party failed to win a single seat in the 2021 Assembly elections.    The BJP registered a notable breakthrough by winning Nemom, Kazhakkoottam and Chathannoor, even as the Congress-led UDF swept to power in the state. In Nemom, Chandrasekhar defeated CPI(M) leader V. Sivankutty by 3,590 votes, while Congress candidate K. S. Sabarinadhan finished third in a tightly contested three-cornered fight.    In Kazhakkoottam (Seat 132), Muraleedharan’s victory marked a significant gain for the BJP in the Thiruvananthapuram region. A seasoned national leader and former Union Minister of State for External Affairs and Parliamentary Affairs, he made a strong comeback after previously contesting the seat in 2016, where he had secured 42,732 votes but lost by 7,347 votes.    This time, he polled 46,564 votes in a closely fought contest against CPI(M)’s Kadakampally Surendran, with the Congress also in the fray.    Kazhakkoottam saw a higher voter turnout of 79.32% in 2026, compared to 69.61% in 2021, reflecting increased electoral participation. In Nemom (Seat 135), Chandrasekhar secured 49,917 votes, underlining the BJP’s improved performance in urban pockets of the state.    Following the results, Chandrasekhar pointed to strong anti-incumbency against the CPI(M), saying the elections were largely about “throwing out” the ruling party.    He also highlighted the NDA’s growing acceptance across sections of voters and called the outcome “the start of a new beginning” for Kerala’s development.    Kerala went to the polls in a single phase on April 9, recording a voter turnout of 78.27%. Counting began at 8 am, starting with postal ballots, followed by EVM counting, with round-wise updates being published in real time by the Election Commission.    While the BJP remains far from being a dominant force in Kerala, winning three seats marks a breakthrough moment, signalling that the party is beginning to carve out pockets of support in a state that has long resisted its electoral expansion.

articles.title: Who powered BJP’s Bengal breakthrough? Meet key leaders behind the historic victory
articles.snippet: From high-voltage rallies led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the meticulous organisational planning overseen by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, the BJP campaign combined national messaging with local mobilisation.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: From high-voltage rallies led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the meticulous organisational planning overseen by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, the BJP campaign combined national messaging with local mobilisation.
articles.body: As the BJP appears set to make history in West Bengal, a coordinated push by its top leadership, state faces, and behind-the-scenes strategists has powered the party’s campaign on the ground.    The state is poised to witness its first BJP government since Independence, with the Trinamool Congress facing defeat after 15 years in power in an election held following a record voter deletion drive under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).    From high-voltage rallies led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the meticulous organisational planning overseen by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, the BJP campaign combined national messaging with local mobilisation.    PM Modi’s sustained push    From invoking Bengal’s cultural symbols like jhalmuri to promising job guarantees and offering prayers at Maa Kali temples, Prime Narendra Modi crafted a campaign that blended local connection with national messaging in West Bengal.    His outreach wasn’t limited to large rallies. In fact, he made efforts to strike an emotional chord with voters by referencing everyday cultural elements and regional identity. At the same time, he sharpened the development pitch, highlighting employment generation, welfare delivery, and the promise of a “double-engine government.”    By combining cultural symbolism, religious outreach, and economic assurances, PM Modi’s campaigns tried to  resonate across sections.    BJP’s ‘Chanakya’    PM Modi served as the face of the campaign. But it was Shah’s “Chanakya-style strategy that helped break Trinamool strongholds. According to a Moneycontrol analysis, Shah emerged as BJP’s most aggressive campaigner in West Bengal, clocking the highest number of rallies and constituency visits. Shah held 66 rallies and roadshows covering 63 locations in West Bengal.    At the heart of Shah’s “Mission Bengal” was a relentless focus on strengthening the party’s grassroots structure. Under his guidance, the BJP  worked to build booth-level networks across constituencies.    Shah promised to seal the Bangladesh border within 45 days, accusing Trinamool of encouraging infiltration for vote-bank politics, while repeatedly targeting alleged corruption through the “cut money” culture and syndicate system. Shah also raised concerns over women’s safety and law and order, citing incidents like Sandeshkhali and promising measures such as 33% reservation in government jobs. His campaign included welfare pledges like Rs 3,000 monthly support for women, improved salaries for government employees, and land rights for tea garden workers. At the same time, he emphasised cultural identity and religious freedom, positioning the BJP as a protector of Bengali traditions, and pushed the “double-engine” development model.    Bhupendra Yadav    Union minister Bhupendra Yadav was named the  election in-charge for the 2026 Bengal assembly polls last year.    He played a key behind-the-scenes role in shaping the BJP’s campaign in West Bengal, focusing largely on organisation and coordination.    Yadav was also involved in candidate selection and alliance management, working to identify winnable faces and strengthen the party’s presence in constituencies where it had limited influence. His role extended to legal and electoral planning, helping the party navigate procedural challenges and ensure compliance during the high-stakes election.    Shamik Bhattacharya    BJP’s state unit chief Shamik Bhattacharya has been a key organisational pillar in the party’s campaign in the state.    His primary role has been coordination and execution. He has also  overseen candidate selection, cadre mobilisation, and booth-level preparedness, helping the party maintain a strong organisational presence across constituencies.    Bhattacharya has also acted as a crucial link between grassroots workers and top leaders like Shah, translating broad campaign messaging into local outreach.    Suvendu Adhikari    Suvendu Adhikari emerged as one of the key architects of BJP campaign in West Bengal. Once a trusted aide of Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, Adhikari brought with him deep grassroots networks, particularly in East Midnapore, and helped the BJP rapidly expand its organisational base in rural and semi-urban regions.    Positioning himself as the BJP’s principal Bengali face, Adhikari turned elections into a direct contest with Banerjee, most notably in Nandigram, which became a symbolic battleground. His aggressive campaigning, focus on issues like corruption and political violence, and push for consolidation of key vote blocs aligned closely with the BJP’s broader strategy in the state.    As Leader of the Opposition, he continued to shape the party’s narrative between elections, keeping pressure on the ruling TMC and mobilising cadres on the ground. By the time of the 2026 Assembly polls, Adhikari was not just a campaigner but a central strategist—bridging the gap between the BJP’s national leadership and Bengal’s local political realities.    &amp;nbsp;    &amp;nbsp;

articles.title: Why Kerala picked UDF over LDF in 2026: 5 reasons
articles.snippet: The most significant factor contributing to UDF’s win was the growing anti-incumbency sentiment against the LDF
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: The most significant factor contributing to UDF’s win was the growing anti-incumbency sentiment against the LDF
articles.body: Marking a shift in Kerala's political landscape, the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) is on track to make a comeback, ending the Left Democratic Front’s (LDF) decade-long rule under chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan.    The UDF has crossed the majority mark of 71 seats in the 140-member Assembly, with the numbers so far showing it comfortably ahead of the ruling LDF.    The UDF's comeback in the 2026 Kerala elections is being seen as a strong pushback against the LDF's 10 years of leadership, marked by dissatisfaction and governance concerns.    Here's why the UDF clinched the victory in this election --    Strong anti-incumbency sentiment    The most significant factor contributing to UDF’s win was the growing anti-incumbency sentiment against the LDF.    Increasing concerns about governance, economic strain, and political overreach contributed to the widespread perception that the Left Front had become complacent after ten years in power. Anti-incumbency sentiment has long been a powerful factor in Kerala’s political landscape, and the 2026 election was no exception, making it difficult for the LDF to retain control.    Governance and corruption issues    Allegations of corruption and poor governance hurt the LDF's prospects significantly. The Sabarimala gold theft and mismanagement controversies, as well as links to the gold smuggling case, created a cloud of scandal over Pinarayi Vijayan’s government. The LDF’s alleged involvement in “cut money” schemes and favoritism in public projects further damaged its reputation, giving UDF a platform to highlight these issues throughout the campaign.    Economic pressures    Economic issues, including rising public debt, salary delays for government employees, high unemployment rates (especially among youth), and the increasing cost of living, were key factors driving voters toward the UDF.    UDF effectively tapped into the widespread dissatisfaction with the economic situation, presenting itself as the better option for tackling Kerala's financial troubles and providing relief to struggling households.    Christian vote consolidation    In the 2026 Kerala elections, central Kerala -- particularly constituencies like Thrissur, Aranmula, Kunnathunad, Pathanamthitta, and Kottayam -- has emerged as a pivotal battleground. Current trends indicate a strong performance by Congress candidates in these regions, fueled largely by the consolidation of Christian votes.    Despite the LDF’s efforts to expand its influence among Christians through welfare initiatives, a growing discomfort with the Left’s ideological shift and political balancing has weakened its appeal. Voters, especially from the Christian community, have increasingly focused on issues like agrarian distress, rubber prices, and minority welfare, leaning towards UDF as a more reliable representative.    Better campaign strategy and promises    The UDF ran an effective and well-coordinated campaign, focusing on policies aimed at improving welfare and development. The “Indira Guarantees” package -- which promised free bus travel for women, Rs 25 lakh health insurance, senior citizen welfare, and a focus on jobs and economic development -- seems to have resonated with the electorate.    Rahul Gandhi’s presence on the campaign trail and strong leadership from local figures like VD Satheesan helped drive UDF’s message home, particularly among urban voters and the youth.    The UDF's success in the 2026 Kerala Assembly elections can be attributed to a mix of anti-incumbency sentiment, governance issues, economic pressures, strategic campaign promises, and the consolidation of minority votes.    As the final results come in, it’s clear that Kerala has spoken for change, and the UDF has secured a clear mandate for governance.

articles.title: BJP's Annamalai congratulates Vijay, hails 'generational shift' as TVK surges in Tamil Nadu debut
articles.snippet: Annamalai said the people had delivered a message against “buying of votes and to dynastic politics,” terming the shift a major turning point.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: Annamalai said the people had delivered a message against “buying of votes and to dynastic politics,” terming the shift a major turning point.
articles.body: Reacting to early trends from the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, K. Annamalai, a leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), shared his views on X, congratulating actor-turned-politician Vijay and his party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), for its impressive electoral debut.    Calling the outcome a reflection of public sentiment, Annamalai described the verdict as a rejection of entrenched political practices. He said the people had delivered a message against “buying of votes and to dynastic politics,” terming the shift a major turning point. Emphasising the scale of change, he remarked, &quot;Whoever gets it done has actually done a favour to all&quot;.    In a congratulatory note directed at Vijay, he wrote, &quot;Congrats and best wishes to TVK &amp;amp; Thiru @TVKVijayHQ avl for a spectacular debut in TN politics. Let Almighty be with you to do what you intend to do.&quot; He further acknowledged the electorate, stating, &quot;I bow down to the people of TN for your verdict. Happy to see in my land, people have risen in one voice and spoken.&quot;    Addressing candidates from the National Democratic Alliance (NDA), Annamalai described the election as intensely competitive. He noted, &quot;it was a hard-fought battle on the ground&quot;, adding, &quot;Congrats to all those who won, and for those who couldn’t register a victory this time, let’s keep fighting.&quot;    I bow down to the people of TN for your verdict. Happy to see in my land, people have risen in one voice and spoken  1. No to buying of votes  2. ⁠No to dynastic Politics    &amp;amp; yes to a generational shift in politics.    Whoever gets it done has actually done a favour to all!…    — K.Annamalai (@annamalai_k) May 4, 2026      The election trends in Tamil Nadu pointed to a significant upset, with TVK emerging as a strong contender in its first electoral outing.    According to available data, the party was leading in 109 of the 233 constituencies it contested, having fielded candidates in 234 seats overall, with one nomination rejected in Edappadi. It had already secured victories in three seats and was ahead in over 100 others. Vijay himself was leading in both Perambur and Tiruchirappali East. The majority mark stands at 118 seats.    Meanwhile, the ruling Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) moved into second place after trailing earlier behind the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam. Chief Minister MK Stalin was staring at a defeat in Kolathur against TVK candidate Babu from the Kolathur seat.    In Kerala, the Congress-led United Democratic Front appeared set to return to power after a decade in opposition. The Congress had won 36 seats and was leading in 27 more in the 140-member Assembly, while its ally IUML secured eight wins and led in additional constituencies. The ruling CPI(M)-led front lagged behind.    In Puducherry, however, the All India N.R. Congress-led NDA retained its hold. Chief Minister N. Rangasamy held onto Thattanchavady, with the alliance winning 12 of the 30 seats.    The counting of votes, conducted on Monday, followed polling held on April 9 in Kerala and Puducherry, and April 23 in Tamil Nadu, marking a crucial electoral moment across the southern states.

articles.title: Top 12 winners and losers of assembly elections 2026
articles.snippet: The NDA managed to gain a state in West Bengal while retaining Assam and Puducherry. Tamil Nadu delivered a fractured mandate with Vijay's TVK emerging as the single largest party. And Kerala voted out the ruling LDF and chose the Congress-led UDF after keeping it out of power for 10 years.
articles.author: Armaan Bhatnagar
articles.description: The NDA managed to gain a state in West Bengal while retaining Assam and Puducherry. Tamil Nadu delivered a fractured mandate with Vijay's TVK emerging as the single largest party. And Kerala voted out the ruling LDF and chose the Congress-led UDF after keeping it out of power for 10 years.
articles.body: From BJP's jolt to Mamata Banerjee's TMC in West Bengal to the Vijay wave sweeping aside both AIADMK and DMK alliances, the 2026 Assembly elections produced winners and losers in equal measure. Overall, the NDA managed to gain a state in West Bengal while retaining Assam and Puducherry. Tamil Nadu delivered a fractured mandate with Vijay's TVK emerging as the single largest party. And Kerala voted out the ruling LDF and chose the Congress-led UDF after keeping it out of power for 10 years.    Here are the biggest winners &amp;amp; losers of the 2026 assembly polls    The Winners    BJP: One more state, one more victory - the party has returned to its winning ways after a brief setback in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls when it failed to reach the majority on its own. A government in West Bengal is a huge shot in the arm for the party which had been trying to carve out a political space for itself in the state. It's also a major ideological boost for BJP, which has usually struggled in the Left-dominant political climate of Bengal. In Assam, BJP gained more ground and is set to clinch nearly 100 seats along with its allies, completely decimating the Gaurav Gogoi-led Congress. NDA now governs across 20 states/UTs out of 28 states and 8 UTs. Of these, BJP is the head of the government in 16.    Vijay and his MGR moment: &quot;Jana Nayagan&quot; Vijay was the undisputed star of this election with his TVK delivering one of the most stunning performances on debut in India's political history, giving both AIADMK and DMK led factions a run for their money. The actor-turned-politician successfully converted his star power into seats, tapping into the voters' historical tendencies to place their faith into celebrities who take the political plunge.    Congress in Kerala: Though Congress failed to pose much challenge in other states, it delivered a resounding performance in Kerala. The UDF is leading in over 100 out of the 126 seats in the state with Congress alone ahead in 64 seats. This marks a comeback for the party in the state's power corridors after being in opposition for a decade. It also helps Congress secure a firm foothold in the south, with governments now in 3 states (Telangana and Karnataka being the other too) as it seeks to keep BJP at bay south of the Vindhyas.    Modi-Shah duo: The winning jodi of PM Modi and Amit Shah successfully added another key state to BJP's ever-growing portfolio, helping the party gain a firmer foothold in the east. Both Modi and Shah led the BJP's campaign in Bengal from the front in the absence of a strong local face, ensuring the Centre's messaging reached the voters and converted the anti-incumbency sentiment into actual results. Shah personally camped in Bengal in the last two weeks leading up to the high-voltage two phases, overseeing the party's intensive campaign to edge out Mamata.    Himanta Biswa Sarma: The Assam chief minister delivered a hattrick for BJP in the northeastern state, fighting the election on a clear cut agenda to target the infiltration issue, which has become a menace in the state. The firebrand leader left no stone unturned and did not shy away from making hardline statements, even controversial at times, to consolidate the core BJP base in the state. Despite raking up some controversies, he helped deliver Assam for BJP for a third time, now with an even bigger mandate.    Rangaswamy: The AINRC led by chief minister N Rangaswamy easily retained the mandate in Puducherry, with leads in 21 of the 30 seats. The chief minister led the campaign from the front in alliance with BJP, successfully weathering the test of incumbency.    Losers    Mamata Banerjee: The TMC supremo proved to be the biggest loser of this election with her party losing the only state where it was in power, raising fresh questions over its future and political relevance. With little to no presence beyond West Bengal, Mamata will have to contend with sitting in the opposition benches for at least the next five years. A loss of election also erodes her credibility as a viable opposition face to challenge the BJP, at least for now. Yet, given her street-fighter style of politics and deep-rooted connect in Bengal, Banerjee is far from being written off.    MK Stalin: The Tamil Nadu chief minister could not ensure another term in power despite taking BJP head-on as he asserted autonomy for his state. Stalin's consolidation of power and lack of structural reforms in health and education sectors dealt a serious blow to his alliance in this election. And with Vijay's rise as the new power centre in Tamil Nadu, DMK under Stalin will now face an uphill battle to maintain relevance and sustain the Dravidian legacy in the state.    Pinarayi Vijayan: The Left stalwart in Kerala could not last beyond a decade in the revolving door politics of the state. His government was weighed down by mounting anti-incumbency, allegations of corruption, the challenge posed by newer players such as BJP as well as criticism over the concentration of power within CPM.    Gaurav Gogoi: The Congress leader who was trying to pose a challenge to Himanta and sustain the legacy of his father, Tarun Gogoi, proved a non-starter in the end with the grand old party relegated to the sidelines in the state. Despite taking the fight to Himanta, Gogoi could not match up to BJP's deep booth-level machinery. He also failed to shrug off the dynastic tag bestowed on him by Himanta. To add insult to injury, Gogoi lost his assembly election debut from Jorhat.    AIADMK: The AIADMK faction, under Edappadi K Palaniswami, continues to lose relevance in Tamil Nadu in the post-Jayalalithaa reality. The party has seen multiple splits since the death of Jayalalithaa and is no longer seen as a credible alternative to the DMK. Despite anti-incumbency, the AIADMK failed to make credible gains in this election and has now ceded its space to newer players like Vijay's TVK. Internal squabbles and alliance missteps also hurt the Palaniswami-led outfit in this election.    Opposition bloc: Finally, it was the broader opposition which suffered the biggest setback in the election. Since BJP's Lok Sabha tumble in 2024, the opposition has collectively failed to capitilise on its brief momentum and convert it into credible gains. The Congress failed to win Haryana in 2024 despite strong anti-incumbency. Later, the MVA failed to wrest Maharashtra from BJP-Shiv Sena combine. The Aam Aadmi Party lost Delhi to BJP in 2025. The Mahagathbandhan was brushed aside by NDA in Bihar later the same year. And now, BJP has wrested control of West Bengal from Mamata, who was seen as the strongest symbol of defiance to the NDA. With BJP's winning momentum running rough shod over Congress and regional satraps, the idea of a credible opposition has suffered another crushing blow.

articles.title: Sugar, spice and everything nice: How BJP is relishing its Bengal victory with jhalmuri, rosogolla and...
articles.author: Raajnandini Mukherjee
articles.body: With counting of votes underway in West Bengal, it seems the BJP is heading for a victory in the state as the party is leading on nearly 200 seats while the TMC appears to be trailing around the 100-seat mark.    As early trends data from the Election Commission of India started coming in since morning, many BJP workers started pouring onto the streets across the country as it became evident that the saffron party was clearly in the lead.    By mid-afternoon, as data showed that BJP was leading in 170 seats, way past the halfway mark required to form a government in the West Bengal assembly which has 294 constituencies, BJP workers and supporters started celebrating by distributing 'jhalmuri'.    #WATCH | West Bengal Elections 2026 | Kolkata: BJP workers distribute 'jhalmuri' and celebrate at the party office in Kolkata.  BJP has crossed the majority mark in the state; currently leading on 169 seats, as per the official EC trends. pic.twitter.com/i93T0tKUn1    — ANI (@ANI) May 4, 2026      Women workers and supporters of the BJP also took to the streets with paper cones of jhalmuri and sang 'jhal legeche' as BJP closely inched towards victory.      #WATCH | West Bengal Elections 2026 | Kolkata: Women workers of the BJP carry paper cones of 'jhalmuri' and sing 'jhal legeche' as they celebrate party's performance in the state elections.    Of the 293 seats, the party is leading on 186 as of now. pic.twitter.com/q6BYkhdqDm    — ANI (@ANI) May 4, 2026          This election in West Bengal, jhalmuri gained special traction as Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while rigorously campaigning for candidates ahead of the elections, made an unscheduled stop at a small roadside stall in Jhargram and asked a vendor to make him the classic Bengal savoury. VIDEO | Delhi: BJP leaders, Virendra Sachdeva celebrate party's victory in West Bengal, Assam with 'mishti doi'. Trends suggest the BJP is heading towards a big majority in West Bengal and Assam.#Results2026WithPTI#AssemblyElectionResults2026    (Source: third party) pic.twitter.com/W7sl4Ogb3f    — Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) May 4, 2026  While this might be all the sweets and savouries that BJP leaders enjoyed to relish the saffron party's victory in West Bengal, for Bengalis, a meal is incomplete without the staple 'maach bhaat'. Many party workers and supporters sat down to enjoy fish curry and rice in West Bengal.
