Chennai, Tamil Nadu: Astrologer Radhan Pandit arrived at TVK chief Vijay's residence in Neelankarai with a flower bouquet in his hands on the day of counting for the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections pic.twitter.com/N6IW4Q36pz  — IANS (@ians_india) May 4, 2026      During exit polls, Pandit claimed that they are going to sweep the election by above 170 or above 140. &quot;We are just ignoring these exit polls. I am sure we are going to sweep this election by above 170 or above 140. We studied very well. We had our personal survey. We are sure about a minimum 45% of vote-banking. It's not between 20-25 per cent... 108 hours to go for the election counting... 109th hour, we are going to take the oath. Our Vijay will become the Chief Minister extraordinarily,&quot; he said.    His predictions have not been limited to Vijay. Pandit has also made striking assessments about key players in Tamil Nadu politics.    He claimed that M. K. Stalin has been going through a difficult astrological phase, while Udhayanidhi Stalin, despite favourable stars, may see limited political elevation. He has also said Edappadi K Palaniswami currently enjoys a strong horoscope.    Looking back, Pandit has referenced earlier predictions, including those tied to J. Jayalalithaa, claiming he had warned of a challenging period before her final electoral win. He has also asserted that Seeman does not have the astrological alignment to become the chief minister.    Drawing parallels with M. G. Ramachandran, Pandit suggested Vijay’s trajectory could mirror that of long-standing political dominance. He has even gone as far as to predict that the era of the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam could eventually give way to a new political order led by TVK.    Separately, astrologer Shelvi K Damodaran had also flagged Vijay’s entry into politics as a “decisive phase”, citing planetary conditions like “Neecha Bhanga Raja Yoga” as indicators of prominence and influence, according to ABP Tamil.

articles.title: 'Keep this video ...': Prashant Kishor's old prediction for Vijay goes viral as TVK dominates Tamil Nadu...
articles.snippet: The remarks are now going viral on social media as TVK is leading in over 100 out of the 234 seats in the state, far ahead of both the heavyweight regional alliances: DMK and AIADMK.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: The remarks are now going viral on social media as TVK is leading in over 100 out of the 234 seats in the state, far ahead of both the heavyweight regional alliances: DMK and AIADMK.
articles.body: Political strategist-turned-politician Prashant Kishor appears to have hit the bull's eye on the Tamil Nadu election results as his earlier prediction that Vijay's TVK may win by contesting alone in the state has resurfaced on social media.    Kishor, who was the special political advisor for Vijay's party, had earlier told Tamil Nadu-based Thanthi TV that Vijay stands a very good chance if he goes alone in Tamil Nadu.    Tamil Nadu elections: Follow live updates    When asked whether he saw any possibility of an alliance with AIADMK, Kishor responded: &quot;Absolutely&quot;.    &quot;The commitment is to go alone, absolutely. I don't see that changing. If he goes alone, he stands a very good chance,&quot; he said.    &quot;Keep this video and played when the result comes in Tamil Nadu&quot;  Prashant Kishor- man who could rightly predict everybody's political future except his own. pic.twitter.com/zCQNCNLoQA    — Piyush Rai (@Benarasiyaa) May 4, 2026      When probed further about what he meant by &quot;good chance&quot;, Kishor said: &quot;Good chance to win Tamil Nadu.&quot;    &quot;Yes, absolutely. Keep this video and play it when results are out,&quot; he asserted, when he was asked whether Vijay's TVK can actually win 118 seats, which is the majority mark required to form the government in Tamil Nadu.    The remarks are now going viral on social media as TVK is leading in over 100 out of the 234 seats in the state, far ahead of both the heavyweight regional alliances: DMK and AIADMK.    Notably, Kishor, who has scripted electoral victories for several political parties, was roped in by Vijay in Tamil Nadu for his debut elections in the state.    According to a report in Deccan Herald, the actor felt that Kishor's inputs and strategy could prove valuable during the elections.    TVK did not join either of the two alliances in the state and decided to contest all 234 seats alone.

articles.title: Supreme Court strikes down Odisha bail conditions involving cleaning police stations: 'Caste bias,...
articles.snippet: According to a report published by Article 14 on March 27, several of these orders were linked to cases arising from anti-mining protests in the state.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: According to a report published by Article 14 on March 27, several of these orders were linked to cases arising from anti-mining protests in the state.
articles.body: Supreme Court on Monday strongly condemned a series of bail conditions imposed by courts in Odisha that required accused persons -- particularly from Dalit and Adivasi communities -- to clean police stations and other public spaces, declaring such directions “null and void” and deeply offensive to constitutional principles.    A Bench led by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi took suo motu cognisance of the issue following multiple reports highlighting the practice, according to reports. The Court observed that these bail conditions were “obnoxious” and reflective of caste bias, stating that they were &quot;ex facie violative of the human rights,&quot; as reported by LiveLaw.    The Court reportedly said, “We are deeply disappointed and disheartened, and express our strongest disapproval at the manner in which the Odisha State judiciary has, in fact, regressed to a colonial mindset by imposing such onerous, degrading and humiliating conditions, which are ex facie violative of the human rights.”    It added that such measures “strike at the dignity of the accused, and proceed on the premise of guilt, which is completely impermissible in law.”    Court’s observations and constitutional concerns    The Bench emphasised that imposing such conditions undermines the constitutional vision of equality and dignity. Referring to Article 17, which abolishes untouchability, and Articles 14 and 16, which guarantee equality, the Court underscored that judicial institutions must actively safeguard these rights.    “A judiciary is entrusted with the duty to safeguard these constitutional guarantees and is expected to zealously protect those who are most vulnerable (sic),” the Court said, noting that over 75 years, the judiciary has strengthened equality as a tool for citizens against State excesses.    The Court also warned that such directions could lead to “serious social friction” and directed that its order be circulated to all High Courts across the country to prevent recurrence.    It remarked that these conditions create an impression of systemic bias, particularly because “no such conditions are being imposed… where the accused are from the privileged sections of society.”    Even if imposed without deliberate prejudice, the Court said, &quot;the nature of the conditions is so abhorrent, cruel, degrading and unknown to the law, that there is a potential to cast a serious aspersion suggesting that the Odisha judiciary is afflicted by caste-based bias. (sic)&quot;    Background of the controversy    The issue came to light through reports documenting that both the Orissa High Court and district courts had imposed such bail conditions. According to Article 14's report, an order dated May 28, 2025, directing an accused, Kumeswar Naik, to “clean the premises of the Kashipur Police Station every morning between 6:00 a.m. and 9:00 a.m for two months.”    According to the report, eight such orders were issued between May 2025 and January 2026. Of these, seven originated from courts in the Rayagada district and one from the High Court. Among the eight individuals affected, six belonged to the Dalit community, and two were Adivasis.    Many of these cases were linked to protests against a proposed bauxite mining project in the Tijimali region. Since 2023, tribal and Dalit communities have opposed the project involving Vedanta Ltd, which was allocated a bauxite block to supply raw material to its refinery in Lanjigarh, located in Kalahandi district.    The project involves a mining lease area of 1,560.40 hectares, of which approximately 46.37% is forest land. It is also expected to displace more than 140 families from two villages -- Malipadar in Rayagada and Tijimali in Kalahandi -- highlighting both environmental and social concerns.    Findings on judicial pattern and scale    Further scrutiny revealed that such bail conditions were not isolated. A Bar and Bench report indicated that Justice SK Panigrahi of the Orissa High Court passed at least 50 such orders between April and September 2025.    These directions required accused persons to clean a wide range of public and private spaces, including police stations, temples, hospitals, village roads, ponds, and even a bank in one instance. Typically, the orders mandated cleaning duties for 2 to 3 hours daily, usually between 6:00 a.m. and 10:00 a.m., for durations ranging from one to three months, it said.    Out of the 50 orders examined, 32 specifically directed cleaning of police stations. Eleven orders required cleaning hospitals or health centres. The conditions were imposed across a variety of offences, from theft to murder, without consistent proportionality, the report said.    In some cases, there appeared to be a connection between the alleged offence and the imposed task -- for instance, individuals accused of theft from temples were asked to clean temples. However, in many others, no such link existed.    One notable case involved a woman accused of cheating and loan default who was directed to clean an ICICI bank branch for two months. This condition was later withdrawn after she informed the court of spinal issues preventing her from performing such work, it reported.    The Supreme Court has consistently disapproved of arbitrary or unrelated conditions for granting bail, especially those that compromise dignity or fairness.    During the hearing, Surya Kant reportedly told the Advocate General of Odisha that such practices were “bringing a bad name to the judiciary,” and stressed that “directing the accused to clean the police station for two months” is not a condition that courts should be imposing in 2026.

articles.title: Setback for SpiceJet: Delhi HC refuses review, upholds Rs 144 crore deposit order in Maran case
articles.snippet: Court refuses to revisit deposit order in Maran–Kal Airways dispute, imposes Rs 50,000 cost on SpiceJet and Ajay Singh.
articles.author: PTI
articles.description: Court refuses to revisit deposit order in Maran–Kal Airways dispute, imposes Rs 50,000 cost on SpiceJet and Ajay Singh.
articles.body: The Delhi High Court on Monday dismissed pleas by SpiceJet and its promoter Ajay Singh seeking a review of an earlier order to deposit Rs 144 crore in connection with its legal dispute with media baron Kalanithi Maran and Kal Airways.    Justice Subramonium Prasad also imposed cost of Rs 50,000 on the airline and Singh.    &quot;Dismissed with cost of Rs 50,000,&quot; the judge said while pronouncing the verdict.    On January 19, the court had directed SpiceJet and Singh to deposit Rs 144 crore with the registry within six weeks against an admitted liability of Rs 194 crore. On March 18, time to make the deposit was extended by four weeks.    Singh and his budget airline sought reconsideration of the March 18 direction on several counts, including financial distress amid the ongoing war in West Asia.    SpiceJet instead offered a commercial property in Gurugram as security and informed the court that the Centre was willing to offer it some assistance.    Maran and Kal Airways opposed the review petitions, saying the issues arising from financial distress had already been considered and rejected by the Supreme Court.    The matter arises from a dispute regarding the non-issuance of warrants in favour of Maran after the transfer of ownership to Singh, the controlling shareholder of SpiceJet.    The dispute started after Singh took back control of SpiceJet in February 2015 amid a financial crisis at the airline.    Maran and Kal Airways had transferred their entire 35.04 crore equity shares, amounting to a 58.46 per cent stake, in SpiceJet, to its co-founder, Singh, in February 2015 for just Rs 2.    In May 2024, the division bench of the high court set aside a single judge bench order which had upheld an arbitral award asking SpiceJet and Ajay Singh to refund Rs 579 crore plus interest to Maran.    A bench of Justices Yashwant Varma and Ravinder Dudeja allowed the appeals filed by Singh and SpiceJet challenging the single judge's July 31, 2023, order and remanded the matter back to the court concerned to consider the petitions afresh.

articles.title: Vijay’s TVK surge shakes Tamil Nadu’s DMK-AIADMK stronghold, signals end of bipolar politics
articles.snippet: For over five decades, the state’s politics has been dominated by a bipolar contest between the DMK and AIADMK. That duopoly now appears under genuine strain.
articles.author: Abhinav Gupta
articles.description: For over five decades, the state’s politics has been dominated by a bipolar contest between the DMK and AIADMK. That duopoly now appears under genuine strain.
articles.body: Early trends in the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections suggest something the state has not seen in decades. Actor-turned-politician Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam is emerging as a serious contender, leading in close to 94 to 97 seats according to Election Commission data and television projections. The AIADMK-led alliance is ahead in around 70-plus seats, while the ruling DMK alliance trails further behind.    If these numbers hold, Tamil Nadu could be witnessing a structural political shift. For over five decades, the state’s politics has been dominated by a bipolar contest between the DMK and AIADMK. That duopoly now appears under genuine strain.    Cracks in the Dravidian duopoly    The rise of TVK is not happening in a vacuum. There is visible voter fatigue with both the DMK and AIADMK, a sentiment that has been building over time. Trends show a “TVK wave” disrupting traditional strongholds, including several Chennai constituencies that have long been DMK bastions.    Chennai has often been seen as the ideological and organisational core of the DMK. For a debutant party to make inroads here signals more than just protest voting. It suggests a willingness among voters to experiment with alternatives.    There is also historical resonance. Vijay himself invoked the elections of 1967 and 1977 during his campaign, moments when CN Annadurai and M. G. Ramachandran reshaped Tamil Nadu’s political landscape. Whether this election joins that list remains uncertain, but the comparison is no longer far-fetched.    The appeal of disruption    Part of TVK’s appeal lies in Vijay’s personal popularity. His fan base cuts across caste and regional lines, giving him a reach that few first-time politicians enjoy. In a state where cinema and politics have historically intersected, this is not trivial.    There is also the messaging. TVK has positioned itself as anti-establishment, tapping into frustrations about governance, corruption, and political stagnation. For many voters, especially younger ones, this narrative carries weight.    As noted in coverage by NDTV, early trends have even sparked speculation about post-poll alliances, particularly involving the AIADMK. That in itself reflects how quickly TVK has moved from outsider to kingmaker, or even contender for power.    Popularity versus preparedness    Yet, the surge raises uncomfortable questions. Disruption is one thing and governance is another. Vijay enters politics without administrative experience. His party, despite its rapid rise, remains organisationally thin. It lacks a well-defined second line of leadership and does not yet have the kind of cadre-based structure that both the DMK and AIADMK built over decades.    Its campaign messaging has largely been moral and oppositional. Turning that into a coherent policy framework is a different challenge altogether. Economic planning, industrial growth, welfare delivery, and social justice require more than slogans.    There is also the risk of over-reliance on personality. Tamil Nadu’s political history shows that charisma can win elections, but sustaining governance requires institutions.    A moment of uncertainty    What makes this election moment particularly significant is not just TVK’s rise, but the uncertainty it introduces. A three-way contest complicates electoral arithmetic, coalition possibilities, and governance outcomes.    If TVK converts its leads into a decisive victory, it would mark one of the most dramatic political upsets in the state’s history. If it falls short, it could still permanently alter the balance of power by ending the two-party dominance. Either way, the message from voters is clear. The old certainties are weakening.    Tamil Nadu stands at a crossroads. The emergence of TVK reflects both a desire for change and a willingness to take risks. That energy can be transformative, but it can also be destabilising if not backed by institutional depth.

articles.title: Who is Trisha Krishnan? Actor visits Tirupati temple on birthday amid Tamil Nadu election results buzz
articles.snippet: Trisha Krishnan is a prominent Indian film actor known for her work primarily in Tamil and Telugu cinema.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: Trisha Krishnan is a prominent Indian film actor known for her work primarily in Tamil and Telugu cinema.
articles.body: Actor Trisha Krishnan marked her 43rd birthday with a spiritual visit to the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple, drawing attention online as Tamil Nadu awaited crucial election results involving actor-politician Vijay and his party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).    According to a report published by News18, the actor chose a quiet and traditional start to her birthday. She arrived early at the temple and offered prayers to Lord Venkateswara.    The visit coincided with a politically significant day in Tamil Nadu, where assembly election results were being closely tracked as counting continued. This overlap added to the visibility of her temple appearance, especially given her long association with Vijay in films. According to reports, she    Trisha has acted in more than 75 films across Tamil and Telugu cinema over a career spanning more than two decades. She continues to remain active in the industry and is set to reunite with Suriya in the upcoming film Karuppu, expected to release on May 14. The project has already created anticipation among audiences.    On the personal front, Trisha and Vijay have long been regarded as a popular on-screen pair, having worked together in films such as Ghilli, Thirupaachi, Aathi and Kuruvi.    Who is Trisha Krishnan    Trisha Krishnan is a prominent Indian film actor known for her work primarily in Tamil and Telugu cinema. She began her career in the early 2000s and quickly established herself as a leading actress with a wide range of roles.    Over the years, she has collaborated with major stars including Ajith Kumar, Vijay, and Suriya, building a strong fan base across South India. Known for her longevity in the industry, Trisha has remained relevant through changing trends and continues to feature in high-profile projects.    With more than 26 years in cinema, she is regarded as one of the enduring figures in South Indian films, balancing commercial success with sustained popularity among audiences.    Political controversy    A political flashpoint had erupted in the state after state BJP president Nainar Nagendran made a personal remark about Vijay, drawing sharp criticism from rival parties in the run-up to the Assembly elections. The controversy began when Nagendran responded to Vijay’s assertion that his party, TVK, would emerge as the principal challenger to the ruling DMK in the upcoming polls.    Questioning Vijay’s political experience, the BJP leader took a swipe that many described as inappropriate. “Poor man, he is completely inexperienced. First, he needs to come out of his house. Come out of Trisha’s house first, then something can happen,” Nagendran was quoted as saying in a report.    He also mocked Vijay’s political ambitions, remarking that someone “who cannot even climb onto a rooftop is dreaming of climbing to heaven.” When later asked about the comment, Nagendran did not retract his statement. “I said it only once,” he was quoted as saying.    The remarks quickly triggered condemnation from leaders of the ruling DMK, who accused the BJP of showing disregard for women.    DMK spokesperson TKS Elangovan alleged that the comment reflected the party’s ideological outlook. “They follow Manu Dharma, which never gives respect to women. Naturally, he will speak like that. That is why the people of Tamil Nadu are against the BJP. They will ill-treat women. They are known for it,” Elangovan said.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Elections: Cadres breakdown, leave party HQ in Chennai as DMK slips to no. 3 in early trends
articles.snippet: The ruling party's downfall marks a stunning reversal of Tamil Nadu’s political order as CM MK Stalin-led party had entered the contest aiming to retain power in the state.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: The ruling party's downfall marks a stunning reversal of Tamil Nadu’s political order as CM MK Stalin-led party had entered the contest aiming to retain power in the state.
articles.body: Tamil Nadu is witnessing a rare three-way fight between AIADMK-led alliance, debutant Vijay's TVK and the ruling DMK. However, looks like it is an early endgame for the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam in 2026 assembly election as the party has fallen far behind in the early trends.    As per ECI's official data, DMK is at the third place with TVK giving a tough fight to AIADMK-led alliance for Tamil Nadu.    The early signs have even started showing gloom and disappointment among the party cadre with many breaking down and others pulling down tents from party headquarters in Chennai.    #WATCH | Tamil Nadu Assembly Elections | Tents are being removed from Anna Arivalayam, the DMK headquarters in Chennai, as the early trends show DMK at a distant third position.  TVK is leading on 45, AIADMK on 41 and DMK on 19 seats, as per early trends. pic.twitter.com/7xPojVMKcQ    — ANI (@ANI) May 4, 2026  The ruling party's downfall marks a stunning reversal of Tamil Nadu’s political order as CM MK Stalin-led party had entered the contest aiming to retain power in the state.    &amp;nbsp;    #WATCH | Tamil Nadu Assembly Elections | A DMK worker breaks down as the party is at a distant third position, as per the early trends.    TVK is leading on 50, AIADMK on 47 and DMK on 23 seats, as per early trends. pic.twitter.com/LRfWXh4og4  — ANI (@ANI) May 4, 2026      The state has a history of tug-of-war for power between AIADMK and the DMK. The two have taken turns with public mandate to rule the state for decades. However, this time, with actor-turned politician Vijay's entry has proven to be a massive disruptor.    Significantly, DMK's win in 2021 marked a crucial shift in Tamil Nadu politics as it ended AIADMK-led alliance's decade-long rule in the state.

articles.title: Will Himanta Sarma's prediction hold true? Trends from Assam support his claim
articles.snippet: On multiple occasions leading upto the polls, Sarma had claimed that the ruling NDA will win 90-100 seats in the upcoming assembly polls out of the total 126 seats.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: On multiple occasions leading upto the polls, Sarma had claimed that the ruling NDA will win 90-100 seats in the upcoming assembly polls out of the total 126 seats.
articles.body: Early trends from Assam show Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led NDA nearing 100 seats in Assam. Although these are trends, and the leads are yet to solidify, it seems highly likely that the NDA alliance will cross the 100-mark in the all-important northeastern state.    If eventually the NDA tally settles past 100, it will stay true to the predictions make by the Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma. Sarma had predicted that the NDA will get '90-100' seats in 2026 assembly polls. According to the Election Commission, BJP is leading in 71 seats and the Congress is leading in 20 seats.    On multiple occasions leading upto the polls, Sarma had claimed that the ruling NDA will win 90-100 seats in the upcoming assembly polls out of the total 126 seats.    &quot;We will win 90-100 seats in the upcoming polls. Congress will get 16-17 seats, All India United Democratic Front (5-6) seats, Raijor Dal (1) and Assam Jatiya Parishad will not win any seats. We will comfortably win Tihu and Nalbari seat in good margin,Akhil Gogoi's party Raijor Dal will win only one seat in Dihing. In Sivasagar neck to neck fight will happen but at last NDA candidate will win from the seat,&quot; Sarma told presspersons.    ECI data shows Sarma leading from Jalukbari. The seat has sent Mr. Sarma to the ​Assam Assembly​ without fail since 2001. The Chief Minister is up against two other candidates, Bidisha Neog of the Congress and Dipika Das of the Bhumi Adhikar Party, contesting as an Independent.    On the early trends, Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi says, “This is just the beginning, we will see how the counting is going on in the entire State, and we will keep an eye on every vote being counted properly in every round.” Gogoi is representing the Jorhat seat. According to the data from the ECI, BJP’S Hitendra Nath Goswami is leading in Assam against Gogoi.    According to the data from ECI, the BJP is leading from 29 seats and the Congress in seven. Bodoland Peoples Front, Asom Gana Parishad, Assam Jatiya Parishad and All India United Democratic Front are leading in five, three, two and one respectively.

articles.title: Watershed moment for BJP as it surges past majority in West Bengal, puts Mamata's TMC on backfoot
articles.snippet: West Bengal Election Results 2026: Despite facing stiff resistance from the incumbent party, the BJP’s performance reflects a major turnaround in voter sentiment.
articles.author: Abhinav Gupta
articles.description: West Bengal Election Results 2026: Despite facing stiff resistance from the incumbent party, the BJP’s performance reflects a major turnaround in voter sentiment.
articles.body: The Bharatiya Janata Party has crossed the majority mark in the West Bengal Assembly elections, signalling a major political shift in a state long dominated by the Trinamool Congress. Despite stiff resistance from the incumbent party, the BJP’s performance points to a significant shift in voter sentiment across the state.    Counting is underway in 293 of the 294 constituencies, with the BJP leading in 150 seats. The TMC, led by Mamata Banerjee, is ahead in 109 seats, indicating a closely fought contest in several regions even as the BJP maintains a clear advantage.    According to official trends released by the Election Commission of India, the BJP was leading in 24 seats, while the TMC trailed with leads in just five. The Bharatiya Gorkha Prajatantrik Morcha, an ally of the TMC in the Darjeeling hills, was ahead in two constituencies, Kalimpong and Darjeeling.    West Bengal’s Leader of the Opposition Suvendu Adhikari asserted that the BJP is on course to form the next government in the state. Adhikari, who is seeking re-election from Nandigram and is also taking on Mamata Banerjee in Bhabanipur, said, “BJP will form the government.”    Maintaining that Muslim voters have not backed the TMC en masse in this election, he claimed that a similar trend is visible in Bhabanipur. “I will go ahead after the ninth or tenth round and emerge as the winner in the seat,” he said, adding that Hindu votes have consolidated in favour of the BJP.    The elections have been closely contested, with the ruling TMC aiming to retain power for a fourth consecutive term, while the BJP is seeking a historic breakthrough in the state. The CPI(M)-led Left Front and the Congress are attempting to regain relevance after their rout in the 2021 elections.    A majority of exit polls had projected a decisive victory for the BJP, with several surveys predicting that the party would comfortably cross the majority mark, reflecting strong anti-incumbency and a consolidation of votes in its favour.If these trends translate into final results, a BJP victory in West Bengal would deal a significant blow to the opposition INDIA bloc, which is positioning itself to challenge the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance. The outcome would carry major political implications ahead of the crucial Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections next year, widely seen as a key battleground and a precursor to the 2029 Lok Sabha polls.

articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari answers why BJP is leading in Muslim dominated areas in West Bengal
articles.snippet: According to early trends, the saffron party is not only dominating its stronghold in North Bengal, it is doing considerably well in South Bengal.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: According to early trends, the saffron party is not only dominating its stronghold in North Bengal, it is doing considerably well in South Bengal.
articles.body: Early trends have given a clear edge to the Bharatiya Janata Party in West Bengal. Although these are early leads, the saffron party is leading in more than 170 seats.    BJP's probable chief ministerial candidate Suvendu Adhikari attributed the substantial gains for the party to a bifurcation of Muslim votes in South Bengal -- a region known to be TMC stronghold.    According to early trends, the saffron party is not only dominating its stronghold in North Bengal, it is doing considerably well in South Bengal. The Election Commission website indicated that the BJP is leading on 32 seats while TMC is leading on 9 seats.    While responding to a query on how a BJP candidate is leading in Muslim dominated areas, Suvendu Adhikari said, &quot;There has been a Muslim bifurcation. This bifurcation is particularly evident in Malda, Murshidabad, and North Dinajpur. In South Bengal and Cooch Behar, Muslims are still initially leaning more towards the TMC, but the kind of 90–95% consolidation seen in 2021 and 2024 is no longer there. There are visible cracks in that support base.&quot;    In the Jhargram constituency, Election Commission figures show BJP candidate Lakshmi Kanta Sau leading by 976 votes. Sau has secured 5,156 votes compared to the 4,180 votes polled by his nearest rival, Mongal Saren of the TMC.    Elsewhere, BJP's Asansol Dakshin candidate Agnimitra Paul was leading in her constituency, while the party's nominee from Suri, journalist-turned-politician Jagannath Chattopadhyay, was also ahead of his TMC rival.    As counting gathers pace through the day, the CPI(M)-led Left Front and the Congress are also monitoring the results in hopes of improving their tally following successive electoral setbacks. While early leads favour the BJP, clearer trends are expected to emerge by the afternoon.

articles.title: Who will be Kerala's next chief minister if UDF wins?
articles.snippet: VD Satheesan emerges as frontrunner, but KC Venugopal and Ramesh Chennithala complicate the Congress CM calculus.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: VD Satheesan emerges as frontrunner, but KC Venugopal and Ramesh Chennithala complicate the Congress CM calculus.
articles.body: With counting underway in Kerala's 140-seat assembly, the United Democratic Front (UDF), led by the Indian National Congress, has taken a decisive lead in early trends, putting the question of who could be the state's next Chief Minister squarely on the table.    The UDF has not officially announced a CM face. Per established Congress tradition, the decision will be made by elected MLAs in consultation with the party's high command after the final tally is declared. But with momentum building and exit polls already calling the race, the succession question has dominated political conversations across the state.    The Frontrunner: VD Satheesan    At the centre of the leadership debate is VD Satheesan, the Leader of the Opposition since 2021. Having played the leading role in the opposition against Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan for the past five years, Satheesan has strengthened his position and popularity within the UDF. Exit polls, which projected Satheesan as the most preferred Congress face, only bolstered his claim.    Vadassery Damodaran Satheesan, born on 31 May 1964, is a lawyer-turned-politician who has represented Paravur Assembly constituency without interruption since 2001. He holds degrees in Social Work (MSW) from Rajagiri College of Social Sciences and in Law (LLB and LLM) from Kerala Law Academy and Government Law College, Thiruvananthapuram, and practised at the Kerala High Court for approximately ten years before entering full-time politics.    He started his political career with the Kerala Students Union (KSU) and Youth Congress, and in both, he held leadership positions. Satheesan has been a legislator since 2001, and is known for his eloquent style and use of logic in policy matters, qualities that helped him become one of the most powerful voices in the opposition.    His case is also being amplified by a key UDF ally. Panakkad Sadiqali Shihab Thangal, state president of the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), has signalled that public sentiment reflected in exit polls strongly favours VD Satheesan as the Chief Ministerial candidate, a position that gains weight as many Congress leaders are seen to rely on Muslim League support to influence the Congress high command in deciding the post. Sadiqali Shihab Thangal emphasised that the support for Satheesan is rooted in broader public opinion, saying, &quot;It appears that the sentiment of the people is aligned in his favour.&quot;    The IUML, by publicly supporting Satheesan, is trying to pre-empt post-election uncertainty by nudging the Congress toward a leadership decision that aligns with its own preferences.    The other names in the mix    Despite Satheesan's frontrunner status, the race is far from settled. Senior leader Ramesh Chennithala remains a strong force because of his experience and close association with the party leadership. Meanwhile, KC Venugopal has introduced a new variable, being close to the Congress high command, Venugopal's entry into the mix has made things more complicated.    Shashi Tharoor, the Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha MP, has also been speculated about, but has carefully kept his distance from the question. When asked about the possibility of becoming Chief Minister, Tharoor chose not to engage directly, reiterating that such decisions are for the party leadership and elected MLAs to make after the results are declared, aligning with the Congress's consistent stand that the CM choice will be decided post-election.    The alliance fault lines    The IUML's open backing of Satheesan has not been received without tension. The IUML's overt support for Satheesan has created a tussle in the UDF. Many consider such a move by an ally to be a harbinger of outsiders influencing internal decisions. Vellappally Natesan, head of the Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam, went further, reportedly suggesting that if UDF wins, it would effectively be the IUML calling the shots in government, a remark that set off considerable political controversy.    Much of the UDF's optimism is rooted in the perception of strong anti-incumbency against the LDF. After two consecutive terms, the Vijayan government faces public fatigue, governance criticisms, and allegations of corruption. Suraiya Shaikh News    What the numbers say    Exit polls suggest that Pinarayi Vijayan could lose power to the Congress-led UDF. The majority of exit polls expected a clear advantage for the UDF, with a seat bank of 70 to 90 seats in a 140-seat Assembly, above the 71-seat majority mark.    The results of the Kerala Assembly elections are being declared on May 4, along with outcomes in Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Assam, and Puducherry.    The bottom line    As things stand on results day, VD Satheesan, a five-term legislator from Paravur with strong opposition credentials, IUML backing, and the highest approval ratings among UDF leaders in pre-election surveys, is the most likely Chief Minister if the UDF crosses the majority mark. However, the final call will rest with the Congress high command in New Delhi, where factors including caste arithmetic, internal lobbying, and alliance management will all play a decisive role.    The next few hours will determine not just whether the UDF wins, but who gets to lead Kerala for the next five years.

articles.title: West Bengal Election Results: No victory rallies allowed anywhere in state as counting underway
articles.snippet: Election observer says celebrations barred statewide during counting as authorities review complaints on agent access to centres
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: Election observer says celebrations barred statewide during counting as authorities review complaints on agent access to centres
articles.body: Special Electoral Roll Observer Subrata Gupta on Monday said no victory rallies will be allowed in West Bengal as counting for the Assembly elections got underway, citing administrative control during the results process.    Speaking to reporters, Gupta said, “No victory rally can be held today,” adding that election authorities had addressed complaints raised during the early phase of counting. He also acknowledged brief technical disruptions, stating that some CCTV cameras at counting centres malfunctioned for 5–10 minutes before being restored.    The directive comes as counting began across the state amid tight security arrangements and heightened monitoring at counting centres. Polling agents, who are authorised representatives of candidates, are required to be present inside counting halls to observe and verify procedures.    Early trends from West Bengal indicated a close contest between the Bharatiya Janata Party and the All India Trinamool Congress, with both parties showing leads in roughly 112 seats each around 9 am, according to initial tallies cited by local officials. The Election Commission of India had not released official trend data at the time.    Separately, BJP candidate Arjun Singh from Noapara alleged irregularities at a counting centre, claiming that neither he nor his election agent had been allowed entry even as announcements were made about opening the strong room. “This is an attempt to commit fraud. We will complain right now, we are going to the observer,” Singh told reporters. There was no immediate response from election authorities on the allegation.    Election officials said complaints related to polling agents’ access were under review. No changes to counting procedures were announced following the initial reports.    Security measures were stepped up across parts of the state, with patrolling carried out using armoured vehicles in Malda district. Counting infrastructure, including strong rooms where electronic voting machines are stored, was opened under supervision ahead of the process.    In other states voting in the same cycle, early trends showed the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam leading in Tamil Nadu with around 55 seats, ahead of the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam-led alliance at about 25 seats. In Assam, the BJP-led NDA alliance was ahead in 69 constituencies, compared with 19 for the Congress-led opposition bloc, based on early leads cited by local officials.    Counting of votes typically involves multiple layers of verification, including the presence of candidate-appointed agents, CCTV monitoring, and oversight by election observers. The Election Commission deploys observers and security personnel to ensure adherence to prescribed procedures during counting and result tabulation.

articles.title: Who could be new Tamil Nadu chief minister? Vijay's TVK springs surprise but trends indicate hung assembly
articles.snippet: TVK is contesting is debut election in Tamil Nadu, challenging the bipolar dominance of the two heavyweight alliances, one led by DMK and Congress and the other by AIADMK and BJP.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: TVK is contesting is debut election in Tamil Nadu, challenging the bipolar dominance of the two heavyweight alliances, one led by DMK and Congress and the other by AIADMK and BJP.
articles.body: Actor-turned-politician Vijay's TVK is witnessing a remarkable surge in Tamil Nadu in his debut election, with early trends showing his party leading in over 90 out of the state's 234 seats.    The majority mark in the state is 118.    So far, trends indicate that TVK may emerge as the single largest party but the state may head for a hung assembly.    TVK is contesting its debut election in Tamil Nadu, challenging the bipolar dominance of the two heavyweight alliances, one led by DMK and Congress and the other by AIADMK and BJP.    Current trends show that TVK is ahead in over 98 seats while AIADMK is leading in 74. The ruling DMK is leading in over 61 seats.    While it's still too early to call the election, trends indicate a strong debut by Vijay, who banked heavily on his popularity to woo the voters in the state.    As per the current Election Commission trends, Vijay's party is ahead in 85 seats while AIADMK is leading in 61. DMK is lagging with leads in just 35 seats.    Notably, Vijay contested the elections solo and did not tie up with either of the two alliances.    This means that in the case of a hung assembly, either of the two main alliances may have to join hands with Vijay to form the next government. However, only finals results will tell who will be the leader of such an alliance.    If Vijay’s TVK emerges as the single largest party, it would give him the leverage to stake an unequivocal claim to the chief minister’s post, regardless of which alliance he ultimately relies on to form the government.    TVK spokesperson Felix Gerard told CNN-News18 that Vijay will be the CM of Tamil Nadu without a doubt, indicating that the party may for the government on its own. &quot;We don’t need an alliance when we are going to form our own government. No need to go with any alliance.”

articles.title: Price Action: Vodafone Idea, Maruti Suzuki rally up to 6%; Sona BLW, Cochin Shipyard decline
articles.snippet: Sectorally, the BSE Auto Index and BSE Healthcare Index outperformed, rising 2 percent each, followed by the BSE FMCG Index and BSE Bankex, which gained 1.2 percent each.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: Sectorally, the BSE Auto Index and BSE Healthcare Index outperformed, rising 2 percent each, followed by the BSE FMCG Index and BSE Bankex, which gained 1.2 percent each.
articles.body: Indian equities witnessed stock-specific action on May 4, with several stocks registering sharp gains and losses amid a broader market rally.    Among the gainers, Maruti Suzuki rose 4 percent after reporting a 33.3 percent jump in total sales to 2.39 lakh units compared with 1.79 lakh units earlier. Hindustan Unilever gained 3 percent, supported by its strongest quarterly growth in three years amid a recovery in demand.    Midcap and smallcap stocks continued to see selective interest. Vodafone Idea rallied 6 percent after the telecom department reduced its AGR dues by Rs 23,649 crore, while Laurus Labs rose 4 percent following a 19 percent increase in net profit along with margin expansion of 400 basis points.    On the downside, Sona BLW Precision Forgings fell 4 percent despite reporting a 16.9 percent rise in profit to Rs 191.9 crore and a 45.4 percent increase in revenue to Rs 1,257.5 crore. Cochin Shipyard declined 2 percent amid profit booking after the stock had surged more than 40 percent in April.    Sectorally, the BSE Auto Index and BSE Healthcare Index outperformed, rising 2 percent each, followed by the BSE FMCG Index and BSE Bankex, which gained 1.2 percent each.    Market breadth remained positive, with 2,570 stocks advancing and 889 declining on the BSE, indicating broad-based participation.    Traders said market action continues to remain stock-specific, with earnings visibility and news flow driving price movements. While largecaps remained relatively stable, midcaps and smallcaps witnessed sharper moves on both sides, with volatility contained amid mixed global cues and upcoming domestic triggers.

articles.title: Global markets rebound in April; India continues to be a key investment destination
articles.snippet: US equities rose by about 9.3% during the month, while India’s Nifty 50 gained 6.7% after earlier losses. Other major markets also advanced, with Shanghai up 5.6% and Japan’s Nikkei 225 rising 11.6%.
articles.author: Anishaa Kumar
articles.description: US equities rose by about 9.3% during the month, while India’s Nifty 50 gained 6.7% after earlier losses. Other major markets also advanced, with Shanghai up 5.6% and Japan’s Nikkei 225 rising 11.6%.
articles.body: Global financial markets recovered in April 2026 after decline in March, supported by easing geopolitical tensions and improved investor sentiment, according to Quant Mutual Fund’s monthly newsletter. US equities rose by about 9.3% during the month, while India’s Nifty 50 gained 6.7% after earlier losses. Other major markets also advanced, with Shanghai up 5.6% and Japan’s Nikkei 225 rising 11.6%.    A ceasefire agreement involving the United States, Israel and Iran was reached on April 8 and later extended indefinitely. However, a US naval blockade of Iranian ports remained in place.    The newsletter noted that India’s nominal GDP growth is outpacing China’s and that Indian equity markets are attracting global capital. According to the report, the downturn in Indian equities, particularly in small-cap stocks, appears to have passed, with improving corporate earnings expected to support further growth. The report added that India’s fiscal and monetary environment remains stable, with expectations that accommodative policy conditions and liquidity will continue to support credit growth and financial services.    According to the report, the current market phase could represent a significant entry point for investors. The portfolio remains largely invested, with a tilt toward large-cap stocks and increased exposure to select mid- and small-cap segments. Sector preferences include energy, infrastructure, non-banking financial companies, insurance, asset management companies, private sector banks, hotels, pharmaceuticals, telecom and data centers, while manufacturing exposure is underweight due to input cost and supply chain uncertainties.    During the month, the US Federal Reserve also kept interest rates unchanged at 3.5–3.75%. The decision saw an 8–4 split vote, indicating internal differences among policymakers. Jerome Powell will continue as a governor after his term as Chair ends on May 15, while Kevin Warsh’s nomination as the next Chair has been advanced by the Senate Banking Committee.    Commodity markets showed mixed trends. Gold and silver prices declined by around 2–4%, while Brent crude oil rose by approximately 8% during April. The Indian rupee depreciated by 1.9% over the same period. Market volatility declined, with the VIX index falling by about 25% to 18.8, according to the report.

articles.title: 'Fans factor at play': DMK's Kanimozhi NVN Somu on TVK leading in 104 seats in debut poll
articles.snippet: Early trends showed TVK putting up a surprise show in their poll debut, with the party leading in 104 seats
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: Early trends showed TVK putting up a surprise show in their poll debut, with the party leading in 104 seats
articles.body: Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) leader and spokesperson Kanimozhi NVN Somu on Monday said Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam's (TVK) early lead in its debut election could be driven by actor-turned-politician Vijay's strong fan base, even as she expressed confidence that the DMK would secure a &quot;good number&quot; of seats.    Early trends for the vote counting to select the 234-member Tamil Nadu assembly have the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) putting up a surprise show in their poll debut, with the party leading in 104 seats amid early trends by the Election Commission of India.    &quot;He has a good amount of fan base. All his fans would have voted for him... Tamil Nadu has a history of people coming from cinema who are able to make it to politics. This is nothing new for us. But anyway, the numbers will play... DMK will win with a good number. We have to see how much of the vote share, what is the percentage of the vote he's going to really take away from whom. That will be the biggest question for the day for us...&quot; Somu told ANI as counting progressed.    TVK chief and former actor Vijay is contesting from Tiruchirappalli East and Perambur seats too, with a lot depending on today's performance and his party's political debut in Tamil Nadu.    Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) is contesting the elections alone, against the NDA alliance led by AIADMK, along with the BJP. While the DMK-led alliance, along with Congress, is looking to retain power in the state.    His main rival, Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) candidate Inigo Irudayaraj, is trailing behind in the initial round, according to early counting trends.    TVK chief Vijay's entry had turned the Tamil Nadu polls triangular. The politics in the state have traditionally been dominated by alliances led by the DMK and AIADMK.    Apart from Tamil Nadu, counting is underway across 823 constituencies in key regions including West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Keralam, Assam, and the Union Territory of Puducherry.    The process begins with postal ballots, followed by the counting of Electronic Voting Machines from 8:30 am, with round-wise results being updated in real time on the ECINET platform and the Election Commission's official portal.

articles.title: Vijay’s TVK surges in Tamil Nadu early trends, challenges DMK-AIADMK dominance
articles.snippet: According to early data as of 10.44 am, TVK was leading in 100 seats, placing it ahead of both DMK (47) and AIADMK (64) at this stage of counting.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: According to early data as of 10.44 am, TVK was leading in 100 seats, placing it ahead of both DMK (47) and AIADMK (64) at this stage of counting.
articles.body: Early counting patterns in the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections point to a major political shift, with actor-turned-politician Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) emerging as a serious contender and potentially displacing the AIADMK as the principal opposition force.    Initial trends showed Vijay ahead in key constituencies such as Tiruchi (East) and Perambur, while the DMK maintained a lead across multiple segments.    At the same time, AIADMK appeared to slip to third position in several seats, indicating a reshaping of the state’s long-standing electoral dynamics.    According to early data as of 10.44 am, TVK was leading in 100 seats, placing it ahead of both Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) (47) and All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) (64) at this stage of counting.    The development suggests that the contest is no longer confined to the traditional two-party rivalry between the DMK and the AIADMK.    The party’s performance in its debut Assembly election has drawn attention, especially given Vijay’s transition from cinema to politics. As per the trends, TVK seems to be translating his widespread popularity into tangible electoral gains across regions.    The state, which went to polls in a single phase on April 23, is now witnessing counting for all 234 constituencies.    The early numbers indicate a possible churn in voter preferences, with TVK positioned as both a disruptor and a potential frontrunner.    Describing the momentum, reports said Vijay has “dramatically upped the stakes in the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections,” with his party gaining ground beyond initial expectations.    If these trends hold, they could mark a departure from Tamil Nadu’s decades-old bipolar political structure dominated by the DMK and AIADMK.    The counting of votes for all 234 Tamil Nadu Assembly constituencies began at 8 am on Monday, amid tight security arrangements throughout Chennai.    Outside the TVK headquarters, party workers and supporters were seen gathering early in the morning, awaiting the start of the counting process and early trends, reported ANI.    At the DMK headquarters, Anna Arivalayam, similar scenes of anticipation were witnessed, with party cadres monitoring updates closely as counting got underway across the state.    One of the key counting centres has been set up at Loyola College in Chennai, where votes for several important constituencies, including Thousand Lights, Anna Nagar, T. Nagar, Mylapore, Velachery, and Saidapet, are being counted.    According to officials, each counting hall is under constant surveillance with CCTV cameras, and only authorised personnel, including counting agents and election officials, are permitted inside after strict verification. Barricades have been erected around the college premises to regulate traffic and prevent unauthorised entry.    Quick Response Teams and senior police officers are monitoring the situation on the ground.    Further, heavy security arrangements have been put in place at the counting centre set up at Loyola College in Chennai, where votes for several key Assembly constituencies will be counted.    The stage is set for the counting of votes in the 2026 Assembly elections across four key states, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Assam, Keralam, and the Union Territory of Puducherry, with counting beginning at 8 am on Monday.    (With inputs from agencies)

articles.title: BJP crosses halfway mark West Bengal counting trends, shows EC data
articles.snippet: The election is being seen as a crucial test for Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, with her party aiming for a fourth consecutive term.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: The election is being seen as a crucial test for Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, with her party aiming for a fourth consecutive term.
articles.body: Counting of votes for West Bengal’s 293 assembly constituencies began at 8 am on Monday, with initial trends indicating a tight contest between the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the ruling Trinamool Congress (TMC), according to Election Commission (EC) data and television reports. The BJP is ahead at 152 seats and TMC at 81, as of 11.36 am, according to the EC.    In Jhargram, early figures showed BJP candidate Lakshmi Kanta Sau in front with 5,156 votes, leading TMC’s Mongal Saren, who secured 4,180 votes. The margin stood at 976 votes at that stage. Sau was ahead at the Jhargram seat as of 9 am, according to the EC.    Officials told PTI that the process started with postal ballots “in keeping with Election Commission norms,” while counting of EVM votes commenced at 8.30 am. As the exercise progressed, clearer trends are expected to emerge as counting gathers pace through the day.    News channels have projected a lead for the BJP in the 293-member assembly, projecting leads of 179 seats for the BJP, exceeding by 31 the halfway mark of 148. TMC is leading on 104 seats.    Meanwhile, West Bengal LoP and BJP candidate from Nandigram and Bhabanipur, Suvendu Adhikari, expressed confidence in his party's performance as counting for the Assembly elections is underway.    He claimed that initial trends show the BJP leading in over 130 seats, while the Trinamool Congress is around 100.    He said the contest in Bhabanipur may be close in the early rounds, but expressed confidence that he will take the lead after more rounds of counting.    Speaking to the reporters, Adhikari said, &quot;BJP is forming the Government. Initial trends show BJP as 135 plus and approx 100 to TMC. Initially, it will be a neck-to-neck fight in Bhabanipur. In the first round of counting, out of the 14 booths, 6 are Muslim-majority. They used to get 90-95% of those votes last time, but it didn't happen this time; there is a crack. I am leading the 8 Hindu booths. From round 9-10 in Bhabanipur, I will be leading.&quot;    &quot;There is anti-incumbency, plus Hindus are consolidated in favour of the Lotus. This is a very good signal for us...There has also been a Muslim vote bifurcation, especially in Malda, Mushidabad and Uttar Dinajpur,&quot; he further said.    West Bengal recorded the highest-ever voter turnout since independence with an impressive 91.66% polling in Phase-II of the Assembly elections. In the phase-I the poll-participation was 93.19%, taking the combined poll percentage to 92.47%.    In the 2021 West Bengal Assembly election, the TMC led by Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee secured a decisive mandate, winning 213 out of 293 seats with a vote share of around 48 per cent, while the BJP emerged as the principal opposition with 77 seats and roughly 38 per cent votes, marking a sharp rise from its previous tally. The Left-Congress alliance failed to win any seats.    The election is being seen as a crucial test for Banerjee, with her party aiming for a fourth consecutive term. At the same time, observers noted that the outcome will serve as a “barometer” of the BJP’s expansion efforts in eastern India, while the Left Front and Congress are looking to improve after recent setbacks.    Counting is set to continue through the day, with more definitive trends expected by the afternoon.

articles.title: Yield Tracker: 10-year bond yield steady after four-day rise; oil volatility in focus
articles.snippet: Oil prices initially dropped to around $106 per barrel before rising again, and remained slightly higher compared with the previous session as markets awaited further developments.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: Oil prices initially dropped to around $106 per barrel before rising again, and remained slightly higher compared with the previous session as markets awaited further developments.
articles.body: India’s 10-year government bond yield was largely unchanged on April 5, after rising for four consecutive sessions. At 9.10 am, the benchmark yield was at 7.016 percent, marginally higher than its previous close of 7.015 percent.    Government bonds ended April close to levels seen at the end of the previous month after coming under pressure amid a rise in crude oil prices and US Treasury yields, although a dovish central bank stance helped ease some concerns.    The benchmark 10-year yield closed at 7.0148 percent on Thursday, compared with 6.9928 percent on Wednesday. During April, the yield touched a high of 7.1421 percent and a low of 6.8648 percent, after ending March at 7.0345 percent.    Crude oil prices remained volatile. Brent prices briefly eased after Donald Trump announced “Project Freedom,” under which the US would assist in freeing ships stranded in the Strait of Hormuz. However, prices rebounded after Iran warned that the move could violate the ceasefire agreement.    Oil prices initially dropped to around $106 per barrel before rising again, and remained slightly higher compared with the previous session as markets awaited further developments.

articles.title: Watch: As counting begins across 4 states and 1 UT, here's how strongrooms are opened
articles.snippet: At the centre of the exercise is a tightly controlled protocol for opening strong rooms where Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) and VVPAT units are stored.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: At the centre of the exercise is a tightly controlled protocol for opening strong rooms where Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) and VVPAT units are stored.
articles.body: Counting of votes began at 8 am on May 4 across 823 constituencies spanning West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Assam and the Union Territory of Puducherry, with elaborate safeguards in place to protect the integrity of the process.    At the centre of the exercise is a tightly controlled protocol for opening strong rooms where Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) and VVPAT units are stored. As prescribed by the Election Commission of India, the procedure emphasises transparency, documentation and layered security.    Before access was granted, officials carried out a detailed verification of seals on the strong rooms in the presence of candidates and their authorised agents, reported News18. Only after participants confirmed satisfaction were the rooms unlocked using designated keys held by authorised officers.    The process unfolded under a three-tier security system: a 100-metre restricted perimeter, State Armed Police at entry points, and Central Armed Police Forces guarding the storage areas. CCTV cameras monitored all activity, with live feeds made available to candidates and their representatives.    #WATCH | Tamil Nadu Elections 2026 | Strong room at Loyola College counting centre in Chennai opened. Counting of votes has begun. pic.twitter.com/IngxfcNhzP  — ANI (@ANI) May 4, 2026      Once opened, EVMs and VVPAT units were removed in a fixed sequence and transported under escort to counting halls, where they were placed on assigned tables. Each movement was logged officially. Counting began with postal ballots, followed by EVM rounds from 8:30 am, with updates published in real time on ECINET and official portals.    However, the process unfolded amid political friction. Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra alleged, “CCTV Cameras switched off in strongroom of 4 ACs… from 23:52 hrs for 2 minute 16 secs. We are awake,” questioning authorities and adding, “you up to your tricks again?”      #WATCH | Tamil Nadu Elections 2026 | Counting of votes cast through EVMs begins at a counting centre in Tiruchirappalli. pic.twitter.com/vMBPFLI651    — ANI (@ANI) May 4, 2026          Elsewhere, disputes arose between party agents. A TMC agent claimed, “They are not allowing us to take files or pens inside, but the BJP polling agents are allowed to take them inside.” A BJP agent countered, “They are not carrying their ID cards… They are creating a ruckus unnecessarily.”    The poll body has yet to respond to the CCTV allegations but maintains that comprehensive measures ensure free and fair counting.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Polls: Can richest candidate Leema Rose breach DMK’s Lalgudi fortress?
articles.snippet: In a largely rural constituency like Lalgudi, this sharp contrast between candidate wealth and voter profile has become a key talking point.
articles.author: Manisha Lal Khandpur
articles.description: In a largely rural constituency like Lalgudi, this sharp contrast between candidate wealth and voter profile has become a key talking point.
articles.body: Among several high-stakes contests in the Tamil Nadu Assembly polls 2026, one seat has grabbed attention. It is Lalgudi in Tiruchirappalli district-- as AIADMK has fielded Leema Rose, officially the wealthiest candidate in the state, against a constituency long dominated by the DMK.    For years, Lalgudi has been seen as a safe DMK seat. Now, it is being watched closely as a test of whether money power and a strong opposition push can challenge a deeply rooted political network.    Who is Leema Rose?    Leema Rose is the wife of Lottery King Santiago Martin, is making her electoral debut from Lalgudi on an AIADMK ticket. .Unlike traditional candidates, she does not come from a political background. Her profile is largely that of a business-family figure, with interests in real estate, gaming and hospitality. Her entry into politics has been strategic—AIADMK has fielded her in a seat where a big push could potentially disrupt the DMK’s dominance.    The ‘richest candidate’ factor    In her election affidavit, Leema Rose declared an income of Rs 9.82 crore for 2024-25 while her husband, Santiago Martin's income of Rs 11.39 crore, while their son Jose Daison Martin has declared Rs 19.56 crore. The affidavit shows Leema Rose holds movable assets worth Rs 139.62 crore and immovable assets of Rs 909.94 crore. Santiago Martin's movable and immovable assets are Rs 3,262.01 crore and Rs 887.36 crore, respectively, and Jose Daison Martin has movable assets of Rs 225.56 crore and immovable assets of Rs 439.21 crore. Leema Rose's educational qualification is Class VI.    In a largely rural constituency like Lalgudi, this sharp contrast between candidate wealth and voter profile has become a key talking point.    A DMK stronghold with a pattern    Lalgudi has long been dominated by the DMK, with its candidates registering a win and retaining the seat in the last three elections- 2011,2016,2021.    Significantly, when the AIADMK swept Tamil nadu elections in 2011, Lalgudi seat remained with the DMK. 2016 witnessed a tight battle but DMK held on. By 2021, the margin widened again, showing the party’s organisational strength on the ground.    While four-time MLA A. Soundara Pandian built this base in over nearly two decades, this time, the party decided to replace him with T. Parivallal, hinting at a possible internal friction.    Why Leema Rose's candidature matters?    Leema Rose brings financial muscle and a high-visibility campaign. But she faces structural challenges like DMK’s strong grassroots presence, loyal voter base, and a history of repeated wins.    At the same time, DMK is dealing with internal friction after dropping its long-time MLA. Any discontent within its ranks could create an opening.    The contest also includes other players like TVK and NTK, which could split votes and complicate the outcome.    The real test    For Leema Rose, Lalgudi is more than just a debut election. It is a test of whether wealth and strategy can translate into voter trust in a constituency shaped by long-term political loyalty.    For now, DMK remains the favourite. But if opposition votes consolidate and internal cracks widen, Lalgudi could turn into one of the most closely watched battles in Tamil Nadu.

articles.title: All eyes on 37 key barometer seats that could decide West Bengal’s poll fate today
articles.snippet: Because of this prolonged political stability, voting patterns in many constituencies began to align closely with the overall state mood.
articles.author: Ria Kapoor
articles.description: Because of this prolonged political stability, voting patterns in many constituencies began to align closely with the overall state mood.
articles.body: With the results for the West Bengal Assembly elections to be declared on May 4, one set of constituencies is drawing particular attention from political observers and analysts alike.    These are the so-called barometer seats, a group of 37 constituencies that have, for decades, mirrored the final outcome of the state’s electoral verdict.    With Mamata Banerjee-led All India Trinamool Congress aiming for a fourth consecutive term and the Bharatiya Janata Party pushing to form its first government in the state, these seats are once again under the spotlight.    What are these barometer seats and why do they matter    These constituencies function as reliable indicator seats that consistently vote for the party that ultimately forms the government. In West Bengal, 37 such seats have shown a remarkable pattern. Since 1977, the party that has won the majority of these seats has always gone on to form the government in the state.    Out of the total 294 Assembly constituencies, these 37 seats account for roughly 13 per cent. Yet, their predictive power has made them a key reference point during counting day.    They are geographically spread across the state and include a mix of general, Scheduled Caste, and Scheduled Tribe seats, making them socially and politically diverse.    Where are these key constituencies located?    A significant chunk of these key seats lies in politically influential regions such as central Kolkata, south Bengal, and southwest Bengal.    Constituencies like Bhawanipur, Diamond Harbour, Ausgram, Uday Narayanpur, and Magrahat East have frequently aligned with the eventual winner.    Because of their distribution across urban and rural belts, as well as different social categories, these seats tend to reflect broader voting trends rather than isolated local dynamics.    How West Bengal compares with other states    West Bengal stands out sharply when compared to other major states. While states like Uttar Pradesh have only one such consistently accurate seat, and Bihar and Maharashtra have none, West Bengal has a much larger cluster of 37.    States such as Madhya Pradesh and Tamil Nadu have three each, while Odisha and Gujarat have five each. This makes West Bengal unique in terms of the scale and reliability of its indicator constituencies.    Why these seats have such a strong track record    The answer lies in the state’s political history. For nearly five decades, West Bengal has largely been dominated by two political forces. The Left Front governed the state for 34 years, followed by the Trinamool Congress.    Because of this prolonged political stability, voting patterns in many constituencies began to align closely with the overall state mood. When a particular party gained widespread support across Bengal, these seats tended to reflect that sentiment as well.    Over time, this consistent alignment strengthened their reputation as reliable predictors of the final result.    What to watch for in 2026    With 294 seats in the Assembly and the majority mark set at 148, the performance in these 37 key barometer constituencies could once again offer early clues about who is headed to power.    As counting progresses, trends emerging from these seats will be closely tracked. If history is any guide, they may once again provide a near-accurate snapshot of West Bengal’s final electoral outcome.

articles.title: Baramati by election result Highlights: Sunetra Pawar wins with record-breaking mandate
articles.snippet: Baramati bypoll ends in a record landslide as Sunetra Pawar crosses 2 lakh lead, surpassing Ajit Pawar’s 2019 mark in a one-sided contest.
articles.author: Moneycontrol News
articles.description: Baramati bypoll ends in a record landslide as Sunetra Pawar crosses 2 lakh lead, surpassing Ajit Pawar’s 2019 mark in a one-sided contest.
articles.body: Baramati Bypoll Result 2026: The Baramati assembly by-election concluded with a historic and one-sided mandate in favour of Sunetra Pawar, who delivered a record-breaking performance in one of Maharashtra’s most significant constituencies. Maintaining a lead from the very first round of counting, she steadily widened the gap and eventually secured a massive 2,18,930 votes, with her victory margin crossing the 2 lakh mark, making it one of the biggest in the state’s electoral history.In the process, she surpassed the long-standing record set by Ajit Pawar in 2019, when he had won by over 1.65 lakh votes. The counting trends remained completely one-sided throughout all 24 rounds, with opposition candidates collectively managing just 4,837 votes, highlighting the scale of dominance in this bypoll.The election was held following the demise of Ajit Pawar, making the result emotionally significant for the constituency. In a rare political development, major parties, including Congress, stayed away from contesting, leading to a direct and clear mandate. Baramati once again reaffirmed its position as a stronghold of the Pawar family, continuing a legacy that dates back to 1967.Despite the scale of victory, a restrained approach was maintained, with Sunetra Pawar urging supporters to avoid celebrations and honour Ajit Pawar’s memory. The by-election saw a voter turnout of 58.2%, with over 2.23 lakh voters participating. Overall, the result not only confirmed political continuity in Baramati but also set a new benchmark in Maharashtra’s electoral landscape.

articles.body: Himanta Biswa Sarma Election Result Highlights: Himanta Biswa Sarma, senior leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party, contested the 2026 Assam Assembly election from Jalukbari, aiming for a sixth consecutive victory in a constituency he has dominated for over two decades. At 57, Sarma has represented the seat since 2001, building a strong political base after his initial defeat in 1996 to Bhrigu Kumar Phukan.Over the years, Sarma’s winning margins have steadily increased, reflecting deep voter trust. His 2021 victory, secured by a margin of over one lakh votes, further established Jalukbari as a BJP stronghold. A key strategist in Northeast politics, he played a crucial role in expanding the BJP’s footprint in the region after shifting from the Indian National Congress in 2015 and later led the party to power in Assam.Academically accomplished, Sarma holds a doctorate in Political Science from Gauhati University and has a background in law. articles.title: Ahead of counting, TMC MP Mahua Moitra's big charge against EC: 'CCTVs off in 4 strongrooms for over 2...
articles.snippet: Ahead of counting, the Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP claimed that CCTV cameras were switched off in multiple strongrooms in Nadia district constituencies.
articles.author: Rewati Karan
articles.description: Ahead of counting, the Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP claimed that CCTV cameras were switched off in multiple strongrooms in Nadia district constituencies.
articles.body: A fresh political flashpoint has emerged during the West Bengal Assembly elections after Mahua Moitra levelled serious allegations over surveillance lapses in strongrooms and launched a sharp attack on an election observer.    Ahead of counting, the Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP claimed that CCTV cameras were switched off in multiple strongrooms in Nadia district constituencies.    Listing specific details, she alleged that cameras went off in four assembly segments — Krishnanagar North (83), Chapra (82), Kaliganj (80) and Nakashipara (81) — for a brief but significant duration.    “CCTV Cameras switched off in strongroom of 4 ACs… from 23:52 hrs for 2 minute 16 secs. We are awake,” Moitra posted, tagging the Election Commission of India and state election authorities. She further questioned the poll body’s intent, writing: “you up to your tricks again?”    The allegations come amid heightened political tensions in a high-stakes election, where both phases of polling have drawn intense scrutiny from rival parties.    While the EC has not yet publicly responded to these specific claims, it has maintained that comprehensive arrangements are in place to ensure free and fair voting.    CCTV Cameras switched off in strongroom of 4 ACs of Krishnanagar North 83, Chapra 82, Kaliganj 80 &amp;amp; Nakashipara 81 from 23:52 hrs for 2 minute 16 secs. We are awake @ECISVEEP &amp;amp; @CEOWestBengal - you up to your tricks again? pic.twitter.com/0dFjtiiglX  — Mahua Moitra (@MahuaMoitra) May 3, 2026      Separately, Moitra had also taken a swipe at IPS officer Ajay Pal Sharma, who has been deployed as an observer by the Election Commission.    Sharing purported videos of a man dancing at what appeared to be a nightclub, she mocked the officer on social media, calling him a “Fair and Lovely babua” and remarking, “Good to see you enjoying yourself... Hope your policing skills are better than your dancing skills.”    The officer, often described as a tough enforcer and nicknamed ‘Singham’, had earlier triggered controversy after a viral clip showed him warning alleged “troublemakers” of strict action if they attempted to disrupt polling in South 24 Parganas.    Leaders of the TMC accused him of overstepping his role, arguing that observers are meant to act as neutral monitors rather than intervene directly on the ground.    The row quickly escalated into a broader political exchange. Opposition figures and parties weighed in, with reactions ranging from criticism to dismissal.    A spokesperson from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) had declined to engage directly with Moitra’s remarks, saying the post “speaks of her own taste.” Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party (SP) Akhilesh Yadav described the officer as a “BJP agent,” intensifying the political rhetoric around the election process.    Beyond the controversy, Moitra framed the ongoing election as a larger democratic battle. Speaking after casting her vote in Nadia in the second phase on April 29, she said, “This time, we are engaged in the fight to save democracy.” She also alleged large-scale voter deletions, stating that “2.7 million (27 lakh) voters have been deleted,” and argued that turnout would surge as a result.    “The remaining voters will definitely vote 100%. That’s why the voting percentage is bound to be very high. It’s simple mathematics,” she said.    She added that voters would respond strongly to what she termed actions by the Centre and the Election Commission, saying people were “voting for revenge because they will give a befitting reply.”
